It felt good to stop for the day, to sit around the caravanserai’s hearth while the evening’s chill bit the air outside. Janest took a seat by the fire and accepted a bowl from a chubby-cheeked girl of six. She’d been traveling with the refugees for three weeks now, keeping watch for bandits and other threats on the road.

Since leaving Kolisz, she’d seen many grand sights, tasted every new dish she could, and heard stories that’d never made it to her little valley. What Janest liked best, though, was meeting people along the way — breaking bread with them, sharing their stories, and learning their songs, languages, and jokes. She’d taken plenty of odd jobs with caravans. Most often, the caravaneers took one look at Final Season and put her on guard duty, but she’d been a camp cook and a child-minder, fixed broken carts and set fractured bones.

She’d only taken her first sip of the spicy soup when something made her hair stand up on the back of her neck. In the darkness outside, a stabled horse whinnied in fear. The refugees exchanged frightened glances.

“Stay close,” said Janest. She set down her bowl and called Final Season to hand. In her wanderings, she’d picked up pieces of many languages. After please, and thank you, may I? and how much? she’d found that phrase the most helpful. Her companions obeyed, parents gathering their children swiftly into a cluster.

The sound of splintering wood and a metallic flash to her left was all the warning Janest had before dozens of spindly-legged silverwights pounced, their talon-tipped fingers latching onto her arms to drag her down. Janest dropped into a crouch, letting them climb atop her until not an inch of her could be seen. Then she leapt, a streak of wheat-gold anima tracing an arc behind her. Silverwights scattered and fell. Those that survived the impact did not survive Final Season’s keen-edged swing when Janest landed.

Still more came at her, for all silverwights share a mind. They had felt their kin’s death and knew where their killer could be found

The grimscythe’s blade split the hearth’s firelight into color-streaked ribbons as it sliced through faerie flesh. Flowers and vines sprang up from the soil beneath the floorboards, tangling around the silverwight’s limbs and holding them fast to the earth.

A hulking, pallid shape crashed through the door, twice Janest’s height — no doubt the fae huntmaster leading this pack. A pair of tusks jutted from its maw, though one had been broken, and its body was studded with venomous, bone-white thorns. It closed the distance with a speed that should have been impossible for something so large and brought a fist like a sledgehammer down on Janest. She had time to grit her teeth and brace for the blow; its impact rocked her backwards, but she refused to fall. Thorns bit deep into her flesh; pain blossomed in her side, close to the scar she still bore from the faerie blade in Kolisz. Faerie poison seeped into the wound, and a thrum of weakness spread like a starburst. If Janest succumbed, the creatures would swarm the caravan.

“You won’t hurt them,” she rasped. “Not while I’m here.”

Suffusing her body with Essence, Janest fought off the poison as her wound knit itself closed. The Fair Folk, closing in with its fanged maw wide open, hesitated. She brought the grimscythe up like a bar and shoved the fae away. It flew backwards out of the caravanserai, leaving a furrow in the ground behind it. Janest leapt after it, dancing across upturned rocks and clods of soil as if on even ground. The raksha lumbered toward her, its silverwights approaching from all sides in eerie synchrony. Janest led them into the night — away from the caravanserai, away from where they could harm the people under her care.

EX3

# Chapter Five: Strawmaiden Janest, the Harvest Exalt

Chapter Five

Strawmaiden Janest,

the Harvest Exalt

Strawmaiden Janest is an Exigent of the field god Ten Sheaves. Her powers center around the abundance of the harvest, honest work, and protecting and empowering her chosen community.

## History

Raiders from the village of Kolisz took the infant Janest from the homestead where she was born and gave her to their High Reavers to raise. She grew up with her fellow field-maidens: tilling the soil, working the fields, and training to defend the village and its harvest. Like Janest herself, many of her field-sisters were also taken from neighboring villages in raids or offered up as tributes at a very young age. Together, they formed a tightknit family. When the raiders returned each winter with newly stolen children, the field-maidens gathered them into the fold, becoming their big sisters and mentors while the High Reavers tended to their education and training. If the field-maidens were like shepherds, the village and its inhabitants were their flock. Their work filled bellies and warmed hearths. When invading warriors poured into the valley to steal stores of wheat and corn, or carry sheep away from the herd, the field-maidens stood steadfast and turned them away with the tools of their trade. The same pitchforks that turned the soil in the spring dripped with raiders’ blood come winter. Winnowers traded their fans for similarly shaped shields. Janest’s scythe cut a swath through invaders as easily as it did through the wheat. Kolisz rests in a fertile valley nestled between two mountains. Once, its abundant fields provided valuable food for the Blessed Isle. Growing up, Janest was used to the sight of tax collectors, Realm soldiers, and Immaculate monks passing through, though she kept out of their way as much as possible. While the soldiers could be cruel in lean times, Janest feared them no more than she did the seasonal raiders.

EX3

### WHO IS JANEST?

While this book’s fiction and illustrations depict one take on Janest, players and Storytellers are encouraged to make the Strawmaiden their own. She has no canonical personality, appearance, beliefs, gender, sexuality, and the like, nor does she have a defined relationship with Ten Sheaves, the High Reavers, or Kolisz as a whole.

Some possible alternative takes on Janest include: •

An ambitious Strawmaiden who deposed the High Reavers and seized control of Kolisz alongside her field-sisters. As a fearsome warlord, she’s conquered nearby villages, forging a kingdom that’s a match for any of its neighbors — though not yet for the Realm.

•

A Strawmaiden seeking revenge, either

against the Fair Folk or the tribute-hungry Realm. She finds communities of rebels, dissidents, outlaws, and those forced to the margins — and potentially, the Silver Pact.

•

A Strawmaiden skilled in necromancy, having grasped the secrets of that fell art in the moment of Ten Sheaves’ death. Baleful as her power may be, she could still be a kind-hearted hero, raising zombie armies in defense of her community or becoming a figure of divine mercy to ghosts in nearby shadowlands.

•

A deeply flawed Strawmaiden whose devotion to community has bred prejudice and xenophobia. Players should plan for her character development to involve recognizing the harm she’s done in the name of community and growing as a person, but that’s not necessarily the case if she’s s Storyteller character.

The Immaculates frightened her far more. If the soldiers abused the villagers, Janest and her sisters could stand against them. The monks posed a threat to Ten Sheaves, the village’s patron god of fields and fertility. When their paths crossed a monk’s, Janest and the other field-maidens performed the proper obeisances and moved quickly along. Even the High Reavers were known to tread carefully, lest the Order’s representatives look too closely at their patron. As long as they believed Ten Sheaves was a minor deity, they were likely to dismiss him and let the villagers’ worship continue.

Over the last year, the Realm’s presence trickled away, and with it, the protection its forces offered. Neighboring villages increased the frequency of their raids. The strange beasts that slouched forth from the Wyld-tainted hills, once hunted for sport by garrison soldiers, now came sniffing about the village for easy prey. Malefic spirits of hill and wood, previously kept in check by the Immaculates, now roved freely to work mischief. Janest and her sisters repelled all of these threats, keeping their community safe. Then the Fair Folk army came pouring down the mountain. Raksha nobles rode at the head of countless cataphracts and hobgoblins in overwhelming numbers, destroying the other villages in the valley. At last, they set their sights on Janest’s home, and it seemed like all was lost. Janest and her sisters were ready to die defending the village they loved so much.

## Exaltation

On the eve of battle, the High Reavers brought Janest to Ten Sheaves’ shrine. Though she insisted she was needed on the front lines with her sisters, the god had demanded her presence.

She walked with Ten Sheaves through fields of golden wheat, listening as he spoke of the gods, and Heaven, and a field-maiden’s duty. Though some of her sisters had stronger arms, or were better tacticians, Janest’s dedication

to her people made

her a worthy

champion

in

his eyes. For

centuries, Ten

Sheaves had

protected

the

fieldworkers so

their work

might nourish the village. Though

he

broke

heavenly law

by

accepting

a position of

worship

and

influence, such infractions seemed minor when weighed against the

heroic step he would now take.

EX3

Ten Sheaves could flee and save himself in the face of the Fair Folk who threatened his people. Instead, he’d petitioned the Unconquered Sun and offered his own life to save the village.

The Unconquered Sun heard Ten Sheaves’ prayer and, deeming him worthy, granted the god a portion of his divine fire. Ten Sheaves imbued Janest with this celestial power, pouring his own life into her Exaltation. Awareness flooded into her, that of the fields and farms throughout the valley, the soil and the streams that nourished them. The god gave her one last gift before he faded away: a massive grimscythe. The god-weapon’s black blade glinted in the first light of dawn. Green jade twisted through its haft, and sockets awaited precious hearthstones to fill them. As day broke, Janest came down from the shrine atop the hill, its stream now dried up, its waterwheel stilled with Ten Sheaves’ passing. She strode out into the fields and, alone, faced the Fair Folk vanguard. With her wicked grimscythe, Strawmaiden Janest reaped the raksha like wheat at the harvest. Inspired by their sister’s bravery, the other field-maidens joined the fight. The battle raged for three days, until Janest slew the Fair Folk nobles commanding the army. Their leadership defeated, the raksha forces broke and fled back into the Wyld.

### Leavetaking

Wounded but victorious, Janest returned to the village, only to find it in chaos. Though the raksha were gone, the High Reavers’ leaders had perished protecting the townsfolk from hobgoblins and horrors that slipped past the field-maidens. The surviving priests bickered amongst themselves, disagreeing over the village’s immediate needs and how to begin rebuilding. Already, before their brothers’ and sisters’ bodies were even cool, they were jockeying for power.

### KOLISZ

Beyond the description presented here, Kolisz is left for Janest’s player to define. This includes its location, the details of its culture, economy, and politics, the role of Ten Sheaves’ cult in its society, and the context for its practice of abducting and enslaving children as field-maidens.

repairs and new construction. Even the priests looked to her, hoping to gain her support in their bids to be named the High Reavers’ leaders.

Had she desired it, Janest might have declared herself the highest of High Reavers and set herself godlike above them all: the priests, the villagers, and her field-sisters. Yet, alongside her love for the village, Janest’s humility had drawn Ten Sheaves’ attention — she wasn’t sure she wanted to rule, and certainly knew she wasn’t ready to do so. During the hours she spent walking the rows with Ten Sheaves, the god had shown her glimpses of a world larger than she’d ever truly imagined.

She wanted to see it.

Like a new shoot bursting from the earth in springtime, Janest realized she’d outgrown what the village could offer her. They’d survived for centuries before she was born, and with the Fair Folk routed, they’d be able to rebuild and thrive once more — without Janest. Her experience had made her bigger than this one village. After saying some private farewells to her field-sisters, Janest hefted her grimscythe and a small pack, and set out into the world.

### Wandering Hero

With Janest’s arrival, the mood shifted. Priests and villagers alike turned to her for guidance. What wisdom had Ten Sheaves imparted to her? What instructions had he given for her to pass along to them? Perhaps, in making her his Chosen, Ten Sheaves had intended Janest to guide them in leading the village.

Creation is full of villages, she learned. Some looked much like her home: remote settlements full of people who’d live their entire lives in the same few miles. Others were bigger, like close-knit neighborhoods in the midst of a big city’s bustle. Still others were entirely mobile, such as the trade caravans and traveling troupes she met along their seasonal circuits.

For the next few days, while she recovered from her wounds, Janest did her best to help her community. She comforted those who’d lost loved ones. She walked the fields and, with her newfound abilities, coaxed battle-trampled crops back to health. Though she wasn’t a builder, the craftspeople sought her approval on

Strawmaiden Janest has endeared herself to many such communities during her travels. She’s acted as a mediator and judge, helping to end disputes among local factors. Bandit queens who threaten towns under Janest’s protection have felt the edge of her grimscythe’s blade, as have agatae, manticores, and a tyrant

EX3

lizard. Always, she pays attention to the community’s needs, whether it’s an old rift between two families in need of closing, or a blight driven from the crops.

### AMONG THE EXALTED

Now and then she thinks about the village where she was raised. She wonders how it’s fared without her there to protect it and feels a pang when she misses her field-sisters. Several years have passed since she left, and often, she finds herself turning towards home.

Though Ten Sheaves was a minor god, his influence limited to the village that worshiped him, Strawmaiden Janest is an exceptionally powerful Exigent. While this is rare, it’s far from impossible: even the weakest of gods sometimes choose a champion who outshines them.

## Character Creation

Janest uses the character creation rules for Abilitybased Exalted designed for Celestial play (p. XX) with the following modifications:

Step One: Athletics, Awareness, Presence, Resistance and Survival are Janest’s Strawmaiden Abilities, analogous to Caste Abilities. Her Charms utilize only these five Abilities (p. XX).

Step Four: Janest receives her signature grimscythe, Final Season, for free in addition to her starting Merits.

## Traits

Janest is intended for Celestial play (p. XX).

### Anima

Janest’s anima is a riot of verdure, blazing in the gold of grain but also in the rich blacks and browns of soil, the greens of rain-fed fields, and the white of the noonday sun. Her iconic anima might depict a gigantic Strawmaiden with a scythe that could fell redwoods like barley, a funereal effigy of Ten Sheaves, endless rows of wheat stalks, or mighty beasts of burden like mountain-pulling oxen or wild-eyed mares. ## Charms

### Excellencies

Like a tiny seed, Janest is blessed with almost limitless potential. Although her Charms are limited to Athletics, Awareness, Presence, Resistance, and Survival, she can learn Excellencies for any Ability. She may pay one mote per die to add dice to an (Attribute + Ability) roll or pay two motes per point to raise static values such as Evasion, Parry, Resolve, and Guile. Janest’s dice cap is (Attribute + [most relevant of Athletics, Awareness, Presence, Resistance, or

Survival]). For example, attack rolls will often be connected to Athletics, reflecting Janest’s superhuman strength; she might use Survival as the cap for a Craft roll using materials gathered or harvested from the wilderness. When in doubt, the Storyteller should lean towards simply using the highest value. Janest automatically gains an Excellency for any of her Strawmaiden or Favored Abilities with at least one dot, at no cost. Others must be purchased like any other Charm.

### Charm Concept: Communities

Janest’s magic embodies the power of a rustic folk hero, a champion of the harvest and the communities that make it possible. Many of her Charms involve Janest’s community — any group, society, or location whose populace predominantly has positive Ties to Janest. She can have multiple communities, accruing new ones over the course of play. When her Charms refer to enemies of the community, they mean any character who intends to exploit or cause harm to one of Janest’s communities or a notable portion of its populace. Whether or not someone’s an enemy of the community depends on that character’s intentions, not Janest’s perception of them.

### Charm Concept: Fields

When Janest’s Charms refer to fields, they mean any collection of cultivated plant life. This isn’t limited to any particular form of agriculture; orchards, vineyards, gardens, rice paddies, chinampas, and the like all qualify in addition to literal fields of crops. A field must span at least one range band to qualify.

### FINDING THE FOCUS

When designing a Charm set, Abilities and Attributes with combat Charms typically have a unique focus, encouraging the character to employ a specific tactic or style with its own strengthens and weaknesses. Solar Brawl dishes out incredible amounts of damage but has almost no defense; Solar Thrown emphasizes gambits, stealth tactics, and winning Join Battle to unleash powerful attacks on round one. Janest differs from Solars in that all her combat Ability’s Charms can be used together, similar to Lunars with Dexterity and Strength. While each still has its theme and tactical focus, there’s more room for overlap between them. Athletics rewards chasing down foes to stay in close range. Awareness emphasizes winning Join Battle and reaching high Initiative. Resistance grows stronger the higher Janest’s wound penalty rises and emphasizes protecting allies with defend other actions. Not every Charm in an Ability needs to stick perfectly to that Ability’s particular tactic, but they provide a valuable framework for fleshing out their Charm set by providing a central theme to build around. Think about how your Exigent fights — whether with graceful precision, explosive speed, or simply by staying in their opponent’s face — and then find ways to express that in their Charms.

### LEGENDARY SIZE

Legendary Size is a Merit possessed by elephants, dinosaurs, behemoths, warstriders, and the like. It confers the following benefits: •

Smaller enemies’ attacks don’t inflict onslaught penalties. (Magically inflicted onslaught penalties still apply.)

•

The character can’t be reduced below Initiative 1 by smaller enemies’ withering attacks unless they have 10+ post-soak damage dice. Such attacks still award the full amount of Initiative damage rolled.

•

The character can’t take more than (attacker’s Strength + 3) levels of damage from smaller enemies’ decisive attacks. Levels of damage added by magic don’t count against this limit.

•

The character can’t be grappled by smaller enemies unless they use magic like Dragon Coil Technique (Exalted, p. 280). Such magic is also necessary for them to resist her grapple control rolls.

•

The character can’t be knocked back by smaller foes’ smash attacks and is more difficult to knock back with magic (Exalted, p. 274).

STORYTELLING STRAWMAIDEN’S CALLING

Strawmaiden’s Calling is a good Charm to discuss with your Storyteller when you take it. Most of its utility comes from the Storyteller providing information, and he’ll have an easier time doing that if he knows in advance why you chose it. Storytellers should make sure that this Charm gives ample warning of threats to those under Janest’s protection, letting the player characters rush to their defense. It can also be used as a way to introduce plot hooks, pointing player characters in the direction of narratively relevant or entertaining problems.

The Strawmaiden hums or whistles a tune that lingers in the air, disrupting spiritual forms.

• She reduces the mote cost of Charms used to enhance Awareness rolls with enhanced senses by one mote each. If all three prerequisites are active, the discount becomes two motes.

If Janest knows Divine Tether Shearing, this influence can also target possessing spirits. Rather than materializing, affected characters suffer −2 Resolve against a roll made to exorcise them that scene. Enemies of the community suffer a −3 penalty instead.

#### This Far and No Further

Cost: 10m, 1wp, 1lhl; Mins: Presence 5, Essence 5

Type: Simple

EX3

Keywords: None

Duration: One week

the Last Stand

Where the Strawmaiden digs in and says, “no more,” no force can make her yield.

Using this Charm requires Janest to spend up to a day walking the boundaries of the line she wishes to protect and spilling her blood at intervals. During this time, her anima rises to at least glowing and can’t fall below this level until she is done. A field spreads in her wake as she walks, demarcating the boundaries of this line. It can be a straight line, a perimeter, the boundaries of an existing natural feature, etc. She can use Soul of the Last Stand in defending this line against an enemy seeking to cross it and waives the cost to do so. If Janest knows Field’s Edge Vigil (p. XX), she gains its benefits for her line at no cost. Additionally, while Janest’s present anywhere along the line, the entire line holds back the following dangers as follows:

Animals: Janest may exclude certain types or categories of animal when she uses this Charm. Normally, they can’t cross over the line; in extreme circumstances such as starvation, they can spend three Willpower to cross it. Magically enhanced animals can always spend Willpower to cross. Disease: The normal spread of contagious diseases is stopped by Janest’s line, including the spread of contaminants that give rise to infectious diseases. This doesn’t prevent diseases from being spread by the deliberate actions of nontrivial characters, but such diseases halve their virulence, rounded down. Enemies of the Community: Enemies of the community can’t cross the line by any means. However, they understand that they can break this ward by defeating Janest and can sense her location along the line. In practice, this means that while Janest holds the line, she’ll face a battle against any invading enemies of the community. Otherworldly Realms: The Wyld cannot spread across Janest’s line, nor can shadowlands spread

EX3

### ART OF THE OX-BODY

Janest’s Ox-Body Technique offers a roughly comparable array of health levels to the Solar version, but with more high-penalty levels at Stamina 5, synergizing with her Resistance Charms that reward high wound penalties. When designing an Ox-Body Technique for your own Exigents, it’s often simplest to borrow the health level arrays of a comparable Exalt type. You can feel free to vary from them if it reinforces your Exigent’s themes or mechanics — a Chosen of the Forge might receive a higher number of −4 levels, reflecting her toughness; a Chosen of Blood whose Charm set makes heavy use of health level costs might receive a smaller number of health levels but more −0s, letting her pay these costs without accruing wound penalties.

across it or open within a warded perimeter. The same holds true for any similar effects, including all environmental Shaping effects. This doesn’t affect the Wyld or shadowlands already in existence.

Weather and Natural Disasters: Harsh weather like hail and thunderstorms and natural disasters like wildfires, poisonous fumes, and earthquakes won’t cross Janest’s line. If this is the result of magic, Janest rolls (Stamina + Presence) opposing the responsible character’s most appropriate (Attribute + Ability) roll to determine if her line holds against his magic. Reset: Once per story.

### Evocations of Final Season

Final Season has two modes: growing mode and harvest mode. In growing mode, Janest gains one Initiative when she parries a nontrivial enemy’s attack. In harvest mode, Janest doubles 10s on decisive damage rolls. Most of Final Season’s Evocations have different effects depending on which mode is currently active. Final Season begins each combat in growing mode. Successfully blocking or clashing a decisive attack lets Janest enter harvest mode. Once in harvest mode, landing a decisive attack that resets Janest’s Initiative lets her enter growing mode.

The Strawmaiden crosses the Terrestrial Circle’s threshold, leaving behind her familiar fields to court the wild secrets of sorcery.

Final Season’s blade is as much iron as jade, dealing aggravated damage to most fae and potentially interfering with faerie magic susceptible to iron.

She may use Terrestrial Circle Sorcery. She learns one Terrestrial spell — her control spell — and one shaping ritual for free.

Before Janest took it up, Final Season was a different weapon with a different name. It was Ten Sheaves’ scythe, as humble as a tool forged by the smiths of the gods could be. When the field god burned himself away to grant Janest her Exaltation, an echo of his divine Essence remained in the scythe, and by the light of Exaltation, it was reborn alongside her. Now bound to her, Janest wields Final Season to uphold the legacy of her god and his sacrifice.

Final Season is a huge harvest scythe of black iron, shot through with seams of green jade. Holding it at an angle against the light of the sun reveals an inscription of Old Realm devotional poetry to the gods of the days and months.

Deepening her connection with the cycle of life and death embodied in Final Season, Janest draws forth greater power from her grimscythe.

In addition to the usual conditions for changing Final Season’s modes, its wielder may use this Evocation to enter harvest mode when she crashes an enemy or to enter growing mode when she takes a full defense. Special activation rules: This Evocation awakens at no cost when Janest uses Final Season to kill a living being.

Pakpao knew something was wrong at her villa before she set foot within its walls. The gate had been pried open with a strength no mortal arm possessed. Broken puppets were strewn haphazardly throughout the courtyards: bodies cracked, limbs bent and splintered, heads staring through unseeing glass eyes. The destruction only grew worse the further in she walked. Standing at the center of it, on the steps of her manor, was a handsome man so richly dressed that he could only be a Dragon-Blood, a huge jade goremaul strapped to his back. He dangled a shattered puppet from a string and grinned at her, looking quite proud of himself. Pakpao’s own face was devoid of expression as her eyes scanned across the garden.

“Goldenseal welcomes the return of its ‘entertainer,’” he said, letting the mangled puppet fall from his hands. “I bring greetings from House V’neef.”

Pakpao’s eyes stayed trained on him as he stepped down the garden path. She’d never met this man before, but she kept tabs on the Realm’s agents. “V’neef Midnight Blossom. Born to pig farmers on the Blessed Isle, Exalted at 14, a graduate of Pasiap’s Stair. It makes sense they’d choose you to shake me down.”

“And here I was afraid your strings were so tangled you wouldn’t know why I was here.” He stood, unstrapping the goremaul from his back. “There are those in my house with grave concerns about your influence over the satrap.”

“Satrap Boru asked me to assist in settling an unpleasantness among the populace,” Pakpao said. It wasn’t a lie. She had many friends in Goldenseal; securing an audience with the satrap was a trifle. “He seemed quite pleased with my work.”

“An understated way of putting that you incited unrest throughout Zhaojūn through your agents, only to then be paid from the house’s coffers to clean up the mess you created.” Pakpao’s face broke into a grin. “I wouldn’t have phrased it quite like that.” “You may think yourself ten steps ahead of everyone else, but I know more about you than you may think. I’ve outmaneuvered you, Puppeteer.”

“Oh?” Pakpao affected boredom as she watched him strut proudly through her garden, gesturing towards the piles of smashed puppets as if they were monuments to his glory.

“I know what you are, Chosen of Karana, and that your strength is in your puppets. Without them, you’re as frail as any mortal. So! I have seen to their destruction here. I’ve cut every string, snapped every limb, torn the cloth, shattered the wood, and burned the paper. There is nothing left.” “It’s true,” Pakpao said. “A Puppeteer with no puppets is hardly a threat at all.” “Then you will return what you were paid and—”

“But you’re mistaken,” she cut him off. “I am not without my puppets.” Midnight Blossom gave Pakpao a baffled look; it was only then that he saw the countless strings of Essence trailing from her fingers. The quiet sound of wood knocking against wood came from all around the garden as the broken pieces of her puppets began moving towards the Dragon-Blood, rolling and pulling themselves along. They swarmed over him even as he swung his goremaul, scuttling up his body and gouging at exposed flesh with splintered wood and shattered metal. As Midnight Blossom continued to struggle, Pakpao approached him from behind, yet more strings trailing from her fingers. She looped them around his body, letting her threads burrow into his flesh and weave themselves into the strands of his musculature. With a tug, she brought him to his knees before her, his face contorted with panic and rage as he struggled to break free.

“You’ll make a fine replacement for everything you destroyed, don’t you think?”

EX3

# Chapter Six: The Puppeteer

Chapter Six

The Puppeteer

The Puppeteer is an illicit Exigent created by a god undeserving of the Unconquered Sun’s gift, an ambitious mastermind who brings her puppets to life with strings of Essence.

## Karana

Hail to you, Lord Karana, god of the Meiyu Coast’s traditional marionette-puppetry; Karana the spider, eight-limbed and brazen-carapaced; Karana, whose glory is in deception; Karana, who stole Heaven’s fire. A century ago, his theater-shrine, the Skein-House, was the heart of Goldenseal’s famed Faceless Bazaar, and his Cult of the Marionette was counted amongst the city’s most esteemed performers. His living puppets danced along the district’s streets; his honeyed words manipulated minster and god alike, securing his prominence by cultivating the district into a thriving cultural hotbed. Then the Realm came. Even before Zhaojūn became a satrapy, Immaculate proselytes converted its royal family to the Immaculate Philosophy and secured dispensation to suppress heretical worship. While many

local small gods acceded to the Order’s demands in exchange for their place in the prayer calendar, Karana was never given the chance. Infamous for his intercession in mortal affairs, Karana faced a Sworn Kinship of the Immaculate godbreakers who scattered his cultists and thrashed him soundly, leaving him broken and diminished amid the wreckage of his theater. The monks boarded up the Skein-House and sealed it with amulets and prayer strips, leaving Karana to rot. Cold with fury, Karana beseeched the Unconquered Sun for a champion to grant him his revenge. But his prayers went unanswered.

In time, Karana’s infamy faded, and the Order’s eye turned from him. The Cult of the Marionette’s surviving remnants, driven underground by Immaculate oppression, returned to the Skein-House, finding their god covered in dust and webs. If it weren’t for their craftsmanship and devotion, perhaps he’d still be lying there today, something he will not soon forget. Karana’s defeat made him more cautious and gave him a new purpose.

### WHO IS PAKPAO?

While this book’s fiction and illustrations depict one take on Pakpao, players and Storytellers are encouraged to make the Puppeteer their own. Her personality, appearance, beliefs, gender, sexuality, and other personal details are left to her player to define. This includes her overarching agenda and the motivations behind it. Some potential goals include:

•

Subverting Zhaojūn’s government and reigning from the shadows.

•

Seeking vengeance against those who’ve wronged her.

•

Leading a Tengese uprising against Zhao hegemony.

•

Abolishing slavery along the Meiyu Coast.

•

Amassing wealth beyond the dreams of avarice.

•

Winning the hearts and patronage of Zhaojūn’s people as a legendary performer or master artisan.

EX3

### The Puppeteer and Her Patron

Under Karana’s leadership, the Cult of the Marionette was reborn as a weapon against the Immaculate Order. By all appearances, it’s nothing more than a pathetic shell of its former self, its high priests reduced to begging on the streets. In secret, it recruits from those who resent the Realm’s oppressive occupation and the royal family for permitting it, and funds its operations through smuggling, particularly medicinal herbs. Members of the Cult have infiltrated power blocs across Goldenseal: government ministries, mercantile consortiums, street gangs, academies, and even the Immaculates.

widower and ranking official in Zhaojūn’s Ministry of the Blue Robe. She met him in Goldenseal and captured his heart; they were wed soon after, the first step of her ascent to power. Daopei’s three daughters with his late wife were wary of Pakpao, suspicious of her true motives. They begged their father to cut ties with her, underestimating how tightly he was ensnared. On Pakpao’s request, Daopei exiled his daughters from Zhaojūn; their fate is unknown.

Daopei spared little expense on his wedding to Pakpao, including a considerable sum spent bribing high-ranking officials in the Ministry of Red Paper to circumvent

the laws forbidding marriage between a Zhao and a Tengese. Knowing

of Pakpao’s love of puppetry, Daopei invited a puppeteer-priest of the

Cult of the Marionette to perform. Karana attended with his priest, watching from the puppet’s eyes. He saw what Pakpao had achieved with nothing but ambition, guile, and cleverness and knew he had found his Chosen.

And then, word came that the fire of Exigence burned once again. Karana labored long to find a god who’d been blessed with a spark of Exigence, eventually locating his mark: the wetland goddess Lyja. Playing to her feud against the Realm, he insinuated himself among her allies and ultimately convinced her to entrust the spark to him, claiming he would lend his power to her own that they might create a mighty champion against the Order together. Exigence in hand, he left in the dead of night to seek one worthy of becoming his Puppeteer.

## Pakpao

The Cult of the Marionette has made overtures to Pakpao, seeking to have her lead their insurgency against the Realm. So far, she’s rejected their pleas, less concerned with the Realm than Karana is and unwilling to dance on the god’s strings. This frustrates the cult; many quietly question Karana’s choice to Exalt an outsider instead of one of his faithful. Karana, for his part, is unconcerned, seeing Pakpao’s independence as a strength that will serve his interests in the fullness of time.

Overlooking the Meiyu Sea from Goldenseal’s hillside gardens, Pakpao hides her lowborn Tengese heritage behind influence and excess. Seemingly kind

and generous, Pakpao is

a political schemer and

the Exigent known as

the Puppeteer, Chosen of

Karana. She has no desire

to rely on her divine patron’s goodwill; she seeks for herself the power she never had in her mortal life, free from the strings that once bound her to the will of others.

### A DUTIFUL HUSBAND

Daopei’s true reasons for marrying Pakpao and his current status are left to her player to define. It may be that he’s been blinded by love and played for a fool, as most assume, but it’s possible the truth of his and Pakpao’s relationship is more nuanced and less one-sided than this. The Charms the Puppeteer’s player chooses at character creation may introduce new possibilities — if she knows Corpse-Puppet Reanimation and Impervious Poppet Technique, Daopei may be no more than a preserved cadaver occasionally trotted out to keep up appearances.

Daopei might also be a supporter of Pakpao’s schemes, though she’ll need to take him as a one-dot Ally if she wants this to extend to abusing his authority within the Ministry of the Blue Robe. It’s also possible that Daopei is a more significant ally, with supernatural prowess of his own that he keeps secret from the Ministry. He might be a God-Blood, a sorcerer, an outcaste Dragon-Blood, or another Exigent. An Exalted Daopei might even be a player character, if both players involved are comfortable roleplaying their characters’ relationship.

her with pretty words and convince her they share common goals. Sometimes he speaks to her through dolls and puppets; at other times, his message is carried by his priesthood. He’s selfish, corrupt, and deceitful, and seeks to cultivate these qualities in his Chosen — though what he prizes most of all is ambition and the desire for power. How Pakpao reacts to these blandishments is up to her player, but Karana will always return with new temptations. If Pakpao’s player is interested in bargaining with her untrustworthy patron, the Storyteller should have him make tempting offers in times of Pakpao’s greatest need: hiding her from a Wyld Hunt in his sanctum; offering her assets and resources to advance her plans that would require significant effort to acquire otherwise; feeding her key information about Zhaojūn’s power blocs in time to thwart one of their schemes. Every favor owed him is another string with which to manipulate his champion, slowly steering her into alignment with his own will — or so he hopes. Even if Pakpao defies Karana or thwarts his schemes outright, the god will continue to seek her out. For all that he thinks he holds the strings in their relationship, the pride he takes in his Chosen and his dreams for what she might become bind him to her; he can’t abandon his efforts to win her over.

The Puppeteer has the power to redefine her relationship with her patron. She might choose to pledge herself to his cause, joining in his efforts to subvert the Immaculate Order, Realm hegemony, and the reigning High Queen of Zhaojūn. She might use social influence of her own to win Karana over to her own agenda or to rebuke him into leaving her alone. If she must, she might kill him. The

EX3

Storyteller should discuss whatever plans the Puppeteer’s player has for Karana with her and incorporate opportunities for her to pursue those goals into the game.

### Foes and Rivals

A member of the Cult of the Marionette’s inner circle, Davian Doll-Eye is named for his porcelain eye, which can see any heart’s desire, a gift from Karana for Davian’s part in rebuilding the shattered god. While other priests of the Cult pose as beggars, the handsome and good-humored Davian moves through high society; he’s recently captured the attention of Princess Zhao Mnemonrai Chulin, second daughter to the High Queen. He slowly turns her against her older sister Feiyen in hopes of seeing her ascend as a High Queen who’ll serve Karana’s will. Davian sees Pakpao as a threat to his power within the Cult and envies the blessing she’s received from Karana; he’s a staunch adversary to those in the Cult who seek to broker an alliance with her. While his piety does not permit him to consider killing his god’s Chosen, he would gladly see her in exile, serving Karana’s will somewhere far away.

Once the Cult of the Marionette’s high priest, Cutter took on that sobriquet after she abandoned the cult, outraged that Karana chose an outsider as his champion rather than her. She’s become an influential figure within Goldenseal’s underground, allying with the Snakefire Syndicate both to cut off the Cult’s financial lifeblood by monopolizing the smuggling trade and to undermine Realm hegemony through blackmail, economic manipulation, and assassination. She longs to see Pakpao dead by her own hand and her Exaltation returned to Karana that he might choose more wisely the second time, but

### WHO KNOWS?

Unless it’s uncovered in play, Pakpao’s identity as the Puppeteer isn’t widely known outside of the Cult of the Marrionette’s inner circle. Others may already know if it would be narratively compelling for them to know, unless they uncover it in play.

she lacks the power to do so, despite her best efforts to acquire it. Moreover, Pakpao’s own schemes pose complications for the Realm and the Cult; Cutter is patient enough to let her rival do her work for her. The implacable Zhao Meirun Hao is an official within the Ministry of the Blue Robe and a longtime friend of Pakpao’s husband Daopei. He’s spent a decade investigating the Cult of the Marionette, convinced that the seemingly defunct order was a façade for treasonous conspiracy. He’s convinced the satrap V’neef Boru to prioritize his investigation, providing both personnel and funding. Hao has no idea his friend is married to Karana’s Chosen. Such a discovery would be explosive — even if Pakpao has no involvement with the Cult, years of investigation in the face of threats and assassination attempts have transformed diligence and conviction into paranoia and irrational zeal. Of course, Pakpao has potential enemies beyond these. High Queen Zhao Mnemonrai Enzei would not abide a rogue Chosen undermining her rule; between the Zhao military and her influence over both the satrap and garrison commander, she could easily marshal powerful opposition to the Puppeteer. The local Immaculate Order — which includes Enzei’s DragonBlooded siblings — won’t permit an illicit Exigent to disrupt the Perfected Hierarchy; such a Chosen must either submit to Dragon-Blood rule and Immaculate orthodoxy or die as an Anathema.

### Anima

The Puppeteer’s anima begins as a glowing colorless vibration like the shimmer of a mirage. As it rises, it becomes an ever-shifting web of puppet strings in shades of silver, violet, black, and white. Her iconic anima might depict a towering spider whose many legs pull Creation’s strings, a phantasmal audience that bursts into applause at Pakpao’s heroics, a blurring overlap of the silhouettes of those entangled in her schemes, or the like.

Anima Effects

• Mistress of Puppets: Pakpao adds (Essence/2, rounded up) non-Charm dice on puppetry-based Performance rolls and can perform unrealistic feats of incredibly lifelike puppetry with stunts. She can pay three motes to use a puppet to take a physical action out to short range, using the lower of her (Dexterity + Performance) or the normal dice pool for the action. She can’t use puppets to attack unless she has Killer Puppet Approach (p. XX), attempt feats of strength unless she has Iron Rod Spine (p. XX), or Shape Sorcery unless she has Haunted Effigy Ritual (p. XX).

• Puppet-Snaring Strings: For five motes, Pakpao can make an entangle gambit, rolling ([Dexterity or Wits] + [an appropriate Craft, Larceny, or Thrown]) against an enemy within short range. Martial Arts that use whips or similar weapons can also be used to make entangle gambits. The gambit’s difficulty is 2. Success tangles her enemy in strings of anima for one scene, increasing his mobility penalty (Exalted, p. 591) by one and rendering him vulnerable to certain Puppeteer Charms. This power is free at bonfire anima.

Step One: The Puppeteer has Craft, Larceny, and Performance as Puppeteer Abilities.

## Traits

The Puppeteer is intended for Terrestrial play (p. XX). She’s especially suited for inclusion in DragonBlooded games: teaming up with a Sworn Kinship of

### Martial Arts

The Puppeteer is restricted by the Terrestrial keyword. She’s limited in her ability to combine Martial Arts Charms with her native Charms. When she makes a Martial Arts attack, she can enhance it with Puppeteer Charms or Martial Arts Charms, but not both, with the exception of Excellencies and Versatile Charms. This doesn’t apply to Charms that are permanent or provide ongoing benefits, nor to actions other than attacking.

### Sorcery

The Puppeteer is capable of initiating into both Terrestrial Circle sorcery and Ivory Circle necromancy, drawing on the darker aspects of her Exaltation hinted at by Charms like Corpse-Puppet Reanimation and Soul-Pattern Acquisition. A necromancer Puppeteer who’s mastered such Charms might even gain limited access to a Shadow Circle spell through a Charm similar to the Sovereigns’ Sapphire Talisman Apocrypha (p. XX). Such a Charm might require her to prepare ornate funereal puppets as ritual foci, sacrifice corpse-puppets to fuel the spell, or impose a similar thematic condition or restriction.

As an Essence-based Exigent, Pakpao pays 9 experience for each spell.

### Evocations

The Puppeteer is resonant with artifact puppets (Arms of the Chosen, p. 16). With other artifacts, she’s neutral with moonsilver and starmetal, and dissonant with the other magical materials.

### The Great Curse

The Puppeteer’s Great Curse manifests through a ten-point Limit Track (p. XX). She rolls dice and gains Limit equal to her successes, under the following circumstances:

EX3

• When the Puppeteer learns that she has unknowingly acted in another’s service or to fulfill agendas other than her own, or that she has otherwise been manipulated or outwitted, she rolls three dice. The Puppeteer loses one Limit for accomplishing a legendary social goal (Exalted, p. 134). Her Limit resets at a Limit Break’s end. When the Puppeteer reaches Limit 10, she enters Limit Break and is overcome by powerful and excessive passions, often rooted in excessive ambition, ruthless manipulation, paranoia, or a need for control. Examples include:

Seeing Only Puppets

The Puppeteer sees others as nothing more than disposable tools to be used and sacrificed as her plans demand. She will act to accomplish her goals in the most efficient fashion possible, sparing no thought for how many of her agents must die or the collateral damage of her actions. Her Ties are suppressed completely for the duration.

Duration: Session. This ends if Pakpao sees how her

ruthlessness has harmed someone she has a positive Major or Defining Tie to.

Tightening the Strings

The Puppeteer feels that she has lost control and will go to any lengths to regain it over anyone and everyone, abandoning subtlety for direct commands, coercion, and intimidation. If others refuse to obey her, she must force them to submit either through social maneuvering or violence.

Duration: Session. This ends if Pakpao suffers a significant defeat or setback as a result of her need for

control.

## Character Advancement

• Turning two significant enemies, rivals, or other opposing forces against each other.

The Puppeteer uses Terrestrial advancement rules (p. XX).

• Upholding a Major or Defining Tie using underhanded, illegal, or subtle means, like infiltration, theft, deception, or blackmail.

### Exigent Bonus

The Puppeteer receives Expression Bonuses (p. XX) as normal and can earn a Role Bonus of 2 Exigent experience by: • Intentionally ceding the “spotlight” of a scene’s focus to another player character so that he can express his character concept in an interesting and dramatic fashion, or directly supporting him in such a moment.

## Charms

The Puppeteer’s Charms empower her not only as a master of literal puppets, but also as a formidable schemer and strategist, manipulating others and planning ten steps ahead. Karana’s spider-like nature is reflected in her Charms as well, letting her climb up walls, swing on strings of Essence, or snare her enemies within silken webs.

• Using a performance to advance her or her Circle’s goals.

### Excellencies

• Compromising someone in a position of power — through blackmail, long-term manipulation, Psyche effects, or the like — such that he’s willing to abuse his authority and neglect his responsibilities to serve her agenda.

The Puppeteer can purchase Excellencies for each of the Attributes. She receives two for free at character creation; Excellencies beyond these must be purchased separately. The maximum number of dice she can add depends on the type of action she takes: (Dexterity +

EX3

specialty) for physical actions, (Manipulation + specialty) for social actions, and (Wits + specialty) for mental actions. Automatic successes count as two dice towards this limit. Static values like Evasion or Resolve can be raised by half her dice cap, rounded down. Unlike Exalted with Attribute-based Charms, Pakpao can’t use the Strength Excellency to bolster damage rolls or the Stamina Excellency to increase her soak.

### Puppets and Crafting

Creating a puppet is a crafting project — typically a basic project, though large or especially complicated puppets may require a major project (Exalted, p. 240). It’s also possible to create artifact puppets with superior and legendary projects; see page XX for examples. Common Crafts used in creating puppets include Carpentry, Dollmaking, or other Crafts appropriate to the materials used.

Creation’s most elephantine puppets — those with Legendary Size, requiring Poppet Titan Mastery (p. XX) to animate — normally require teams of puppeteers to operate. They are exceedingly rare, typically seen only at major festivals, certain religious ceremonies, and the entertainment of the exceedingly wealthy. Creating a Legendary Size puppet is a mundane superior project (Exalted, p. 241) Corpse-Puppet Reanimation (p. XX) lets Pakpao animate zombies as puppets; Statue-Awakening Strings (p. XX) lets her animate various inanimate objects. When Pakpao uses Puppeteer Charms that use crafting projects to improve her puppets, she uses Medicine for zombie puppets and the appropriate Craft for animated objects.

### Defense

While grappling an entangled enemy (p. XX), Pakpao can use this Charm on her turn to trap him inside her shadow for the remainder of the clinch. Pakpao doesn’t suffer any penalties for grappling him and she doesn’t lose rounds of control for being attacked or damaged by other enemies. The only actions she can take against him are holds and drags; doing so only costs her one round of control. The only actions her victim can take from within her shadow are attacks and influence rolls against her, actions to interact with objects stored using Jumbled Toy Chest Silhouettes, or mental actions. The victim’s disappearance goes unwitnessed by other characters and he can’t be detected within the shadow except by those capable of perceiving dematerialized characters. Likewise, other characters are incapable of attacking him or the like unless they use magic to interact with the dematerialized.

If Pakpao knows Living Shadow Pantomime (p. XX), she may use it reflexively with this Charm, animating her victim’s shadow without needing to roll. It can attack him without needing magic to strike the dematerialized.

EX3

### SELF-STRUNG MARIONETTE ANATOMY AND POWER LEVEL

Self-Strung Marionette Anatomy’s repurchase offers a defense against crippling injuries that’s even more absolute than the best that Solars get, Unbreakable Warrior’s Mastery (Exalted, p. 378), even though the Puppeteer is weaker. Why does Pakpao get such a strong Charm? Being able to detach and control her limbs is a flavorful combination of her core themes of puppetry and the extensive bodily transformations of the Charm’s

prerequisites. Being able to control your own severed limbs is such a logical (and exciting!) countermeasure

to crippling injuries that it makes sense to stretch the limits for Pakpao here. It’s also purely defensive and personal in scale, making it much less likely that this disparity will ruin a player’s fun or have unwanted consequences on the setting. Finally, it’s both more expensive than Unbreakable Warrior’s Mastery and has a higher Essence minimum and more prerequisites, as appropriate for a more comprehensive defense.

Pakpao detaches a body part, which remains animated and mobile. It’s not an independent character — she must take any actions she wishes the body part to perform (and can use Charms to benefit them), and attacks against it are resolved as attacks against her. In all other respects, it’s treated as an animated puppet (p. XX), including range limits. While that body part is detached, Pakpao suffers the effects of a corresponding crippling injury (Exalted, p. 201) on actions impeded by her rearranged anatomy. She can reattach the body part with a miscellaneous action. If Pakpao is separated from the detached body part — e.g., if an enemy grapples it, drags it beyond the range of her puppetry, and then runs off with it — it won’t decay or deteriorate as long as this Charm remains active. If she ends it prematurely, she loses the option to reattach the body part and it decays normally. This Charm can’t be forcibly ended by any means; only Pakpao’s player can choose to end it.

She can also use this Charm to enhance her movement along other ropes, wires, or threads, like maneuvering through a ship’s rigging, walking a tightrope, or escaping a spider’s web. ## Artifact Puppets

While the Puppeteer can lay claim to all manner of mundane puppets — and expand the meaning of “puppet” to encompass corpses, shadows, and statues — some of her most powerful feats may require her to create or retrieve unique, magical puppets, each a storied artifact in its own right. Three examples follow here, crafted in ages past by artisans who could never anticipate how their creations might function in the hands of Creation’s true Puppeteer. Other puppet

### Okyi, the Infinite Doll (Moonsilver Puppet, Artifact •••)

artifacts exist throughout the world, and more yet wait to be either commissioned or created by the Puppeteer herself.

Doll. None of these copies are quite as large as the original and each has its own unique design and aesthetic flourishes.

Artifact puppets typically cost three motes to attune. When Pakpao uses Living Puppet Performance (p. XX) on an attuned artifact puppet, its cost is reduced by three motes.

Attuning to Okyi costs three motes. It has the following traits while animated:

Hundredfold

(Starmetal Puppet, Artifact ••••)

Hundredfold is, at first glance, a large, folded sheet of pristine blue paper. Closer inspection reveals that it is unnaturally pristine, that it has no fixed size, and that its edges are gilt with razor-sharp starmetal. Its origins are murky even to Sidereal historians: some believe it to be a memorandum that circulated through the Celestial Bureaucracy for a century before it awakened to consciousness; others a weapon created by Kolos, the Scroll-Case Lion, either at a sorcerer’s behest or for their own indecipherable reasons.

Hundredfold can be folded and unfolded into intricate origami shapes far beyond the limits of ordinary paper, but it exhibits a hint of mischievous self-awareness even while it isn’t animated; it may unfold itself from shapes it dislikes or correct errors made by its master with silent superciliousness. While animated with Living Puppet Performance, it typically folds itself into a tiny paper doll with a jellyfish-like shape. Attuning to Hundredfold costs three motes. Blazing Fang Smile

(Red Jade Puppet, Artifact •••••)

Originally commissioned by Shogun Taharu Nibona for an elaborate festival commemorating her consolidation of power across the Blessed Isle, Blazing Fang Smile is a dragon-puppet nearly thirty feet long, wrought from red jade and the silk of countless anuhles. A troupe of Dragon-Blooded performers and their mortal assistant brought the dragon to life in a performance to celebrate their shogun. The festival continued to be observed even after Nibona fell to the Pigsty Coup, used to legitimize successive warlords’ claims to being shogun. The Great Contagion extinguished this tradition, and Blazing Fang Smile has since been lost to history.

“Never challenge the Downcast Eyes,” Sabriye’s aunt had warned her. “Of all the rats in Wu-Jian, they’re the nastiest by far. Not even rats,” she’d corrected herself, “they’re like mice. Meaner than rats, you know. Bolder. That’s why savants use them in their studies, alchemists make ‘em lap up potions for their experiments. They don’t show fear, and they’re more foolish for it. The mice, not the Downcast Eyes.”

Sabriye was forced to agree with her aunt, years later. The Downcast Eye who’d come to stymie her investigations into the cult had indeed been the subject of some experimentation. The youth’s muscles bulged unseemly, channeling some sort of hell-sent Essence in order to swell so. His leg, so like the tree trunks Sabriye had once heard described somewhere in a story, smashed to splinters the beam that supported the roof she stood upon. The roof cast itself downward, and Sabriye along with it. A heartbeat later, he was upon her. She could actually see his heart clench and unclench, molten-bright beneath his translucent, smoke-blackened skin. His next blow was faster than the first, and she went spinning into the catwalks and through suspended bridges beyond their battlegrounds. Down she fell, deeper into the levels of Wu-Jian.

She might have touched the very ground beneath the city, the dirty floor that had not seen sunlight beyond her own in decades. But a tarp fluttered loose from a shop; and a rope’s knot slipped, coils spiraling into the abyss after her; and the hard wooden walls that would have broken her gently warped to absorb her impact and flung her back out to tarp and rope and safety, wrapping her in the city’s embrace. Hers was a daystar that fell to earth not with a bang, but with a whimper, in an open-air eatery serving an entire neighborhood with skewers of charred and dubious meat. “You said you wouldn’t do this again after the goblin whale,” Sabriye whispered to the darkness, under the deafening tones of the youth’s roar and the thousands screaming in terror at the battle. Even this far below, she heard his thundering footfalls and the demon’s power that dwelled within him, drowning out all sound. And yet, she was heard.

“I said that, yeah,” Revana Quin answered. “But you knew I was lying, and here we are.” The older Exalt was all hard lines and crooked smiles, wearing simple leggings and a tunic from some local shop, Sabriye knew. She stepped out from behind a cart selling fried squid balls and pork buns, placing herself between the gently wrapped younger Exalt and the people being flung high into the air by the rapidly approaching Downcast Eye.

He did not forget his hard-won training in his demonic rage. The youth corkscrewed his fist to put more power from his swollen biceps into the blow. Revana Quin’s rear foot and upper body swept back as she began to pivot, moving fast, but not fast enough. His fist did not shatter her sternum and punch a hole to her heart but connected insteadwith the side of her chin.

Sabriye yelped as the side of a residential structure on the other side of the two fighters crumbled in the force of the blow. It collapsed, revealing a honeycombed nest of shocked families in various states of relaxation. Revana Quin was unmoved, smiling, and even the youth was somewhat nonplussed by the response. He responded with a second mighty blow, this one a kick tracing the arc of a rainbow, meant to shatter her knees. And yet when his foot stopped upon her outstretched joint, it was the eatery itself that shattered, splintering downward and scattering porcelain and bamboo across the walkways to tumble down as Sabriye had.

“A little help?” Revana’s voice was more plaintive than her demeanor let on. Sabriye shook herself loose from the tarp, dropping to the ground and freed her daggers. There was no rest in Wu-Jian, not for the wicked and not for the righteous.

# Chapter Seven: The Architects

Chapter Seven

The Architects

As cities form and grow, they shelter not only mortals, but also the myriad gods who oversee the things of city life — gods of markets, neighborhoods, streets, and buildings. The ranks of the divine also swell with gods who oversee discord between neighbors, privyspread illnesses, and the dark alleys where contraband is bought and sold. Foremost among these is the city father, god of the city itself — and above even him is Wun Ja, Goddess of the Shining Metropolis, She Who Hath Laid Ten Thousand Bricks.

The Architects are Exigents who are Chosen by both Wun Ja and a city father, empowered as a hero and champion for a city. To them, the city isn’t just home, but a purpose, a confidante, a weapon, and countless allies and informants. Woe betide any who trifles with her on her turf, for an Architect has myriad ways to excise a threat to her city.

## Chosen of Wun Ja

Wun Ja was once one of the greatest gods. In the bygone First Age, the Exalted built city upon magnificent city across Creation’s face, many of which eclipsed the Second Age’s greatest metropolises. Wun Ja’s standing in Heaven has fallen, yet she retains many connections from better days and has leaned upon them to buoy her fortunes. She’s traded countless favors and broken law after law to preserve her divine portfolio. Though her methods may be corrupt, her conviction in upholding the well-being of cities won her the flame of the Exigence when she cried out to the Unconquered Sun to help save a city on the verge of annihilation. Wun Ja’s Chosen are many compared to other Exigents, though still rare within Creation. Rather than empowering each Exaltation herself and risking her own destruction, Wun Ja chooses an Architect through a city father, who bears the brunt of diminishment for her. Unlike other Exigents created by multiple gods, the shared nature of an Architect’s patrons and their divine purviews brings their Essence into harmony, avoiding the problems that normally befall

EX3

joint Exigents. While ultimately empowered by Wun Ja, each Architect is uniquely shaped by the city she’s spiritually connected to. The Architect of Azure might be a pirate warlord whose magic is as much of her fleet as of the streets; the Architect of Dajaz might be a sybarite to match even the most besotted Cynis scion, quietly ruling her city’s famous underworld with an iron fist. The city god chooses someone who exemplifies their city’s nature, for good or for ill — and the god rarely gives consideration to mortal authorities’ best interests and desires.

Architects are Chosen to protect cities against threats from within and without, to help expand cities by conquest or diplomacy, to forge ties of diplomacy and commerce between cities, to overthrow corrupt or ineffective municipal governments, to lead urban cultural and intellectual movements to greatness, and more. Once the crisis they were created for is past, the Architects find themselves potentially beholden to two masters — while Wun Ja and the city fathers share much in common, they still have their own ambitions and may find themselves at cross-purposes; which of their patrons, if either, the Architect sides with can play a significant role in her days to come.

### City Fathers and Architects

A city father’s role within the Celestial Bureaucracy is to oversee her city and send occasional reports to the Bureau of Humanity. Heavenly law prohibits city gods from directly ruling over their cities, though plenty corruptly exert their influence on a city’s mortal governance or rule outright in defiance of a law with few left to enforce it. They often take after their cities. In part, this is a numinous manifestation of their divine office, but even beyond that, one cannot live in and be the god of a place without being in some way influenced by its culture.

Enjora is the city mother of Imensc, a fortified haven carved into the stone and ice of a cliff near Mela’s Fangs by the nomadic peoples who first settled the

area. She’s an implacable protector of her city but glacially slow-moving, occasionally overlooking important affairs that happen too quickly for her to notice, like sicknesses and sea raids. An Architect of Imensc might be Chosen to confront such a peril to the city, a steadfast paragon and watcher from the walls who embodies the fortress-city’s strength and can endure the icy wastes beyond it, focusing on the Attributes of Perception, Stamina, and Strength.

Ato-Prin is city parent of Atossok, a trade-city built around a Southwestern oasis. Clothed in colorful batiks and adorned with sparkling jewels, they’re a striking presence on the city’s market days and festivities. Though

the Diamond Road trade

route has made both

Atossok and Ato-Prin

very wealthy, it also

brings foreign influences aplenty; the city’s baths ran red with

the

blood of trade delegations

during the infamous massacres that stain the city’s history. Ato-Prin keeps watch over the city’s peace but is ill-versed in the schemes and skullduggery plied by foreign and Atossoki merchants alike. An Architect of Atossok might possess supernal power in this arena, able to deal with cutthroat merchants on their own terms, focusing

on the Attributes of Dexterity, Manipulation, Wits.

the divide between species. The current city father, Far-Flung Clarion, is a nostalgia-ridden romantic who walks the ruined city’s streets to mourn its lost greatness. He favors the Dragon Kings over mortals, taking a saurian form wreathed with flaming glyphs from their High Holy Speech. While he has little predilection toward Exalting a human champion, circumstances may force his hand to protect his cherished ruins and Dragon Kings. An Architect of Hadarath could intercede between communities to bring humans and Dragon Kings closer together or exemplify the city’s intellectual and philosophical legacy to stave off threats, focusing on the Attributes of Charisma, Intelligence, and Stamina.

### Brick by Brick

Though each Architect

reflects the city that empowers her, they’re all bound together by Wun

Ja’s Essence and by the idea

that is the idealized city. Still, no two Architects are wholly identical. As city gods take on their cities’ natures and qualities, so too do those natures and qualities express themselves in their Architects’ magic. And while they may draw upon that magic in any city, and even outside of one to a certain extent, they’re at their most puissant within the city they were Chosen to serve.

An Architect is often known by her city’s populace; beloved, revered, and sometimes even

worshipped as part of her city god’s cult practice (though

not in those cities where the Immaculate Order is strong).

Others remain hidden or take

pains to conceal their identity when acting publicly, the better to act quietly on their patrons’ behalf.

Hadarath, found in the Great

Western Ocean’s Spindrift

Archipelago, is a ruined city of the First Age, populated by a small community of humans

seeking shelter amid the ruins as well as a larger population of Dragon Kings, prehuman saurians whose ancestors founded Hadarath and other great cities and kingdoms. In the Second Age, most Dragon Kings are still young by their species’ standards, yet to awaken to their full mental and spiritual potential. Hadarath’s Dragon Kings largely disregard its human populace but have occasional dealings with them: commerce, culture, religion, crime, and romance bridge

The Immaculate Order favors Architects willing to embrace the Philosophy and work to uphold order. Few know a city as well as an Architect, and few can root out corruption, malfeasance, and treason so well. When Architects actively oppose Immaculate teachings, the Order attempts to eliminate them or bring them to heel.

To help pick Foundation Attributes for your home city, the following are a list of traits and city features associated with each Attribute.

## Character Creation

Architects use the character creation rules for Attribute-based Exalted designed for Terrestrial play (p. XX) with the following modifications: Step One: In addition to coming up with your character concept, you’ll also determine which city she’s the Architect of — her home city. Choose three Attributes that best fit your vision of the city, the Foundation Attributes that your Architect has an inherent affinity for, as well as one Favored Attribute. Additionally, choose one magical material that best fits your vision of the city. If you choose jade, narrow it down to a single color (p. XX). Step Two: You receive the three Foundation Attributes you chose for your home city, plus one Favored Attribute. At least one of your Foundation or Favored Attributes must be in your primary category, and at least one must be in your secondary category. Step Five: Choose 15 Charms in addition to two Excellencies. Each Excellency must be in a Foundation or Favored Attribute.

Step Six: Architects don’t have a Limit Trigger. Step Seven: Architects spend bonus points as follows:

### Anima

The anima banners of Architects vary widely among individuals, always shining in colors that are emblematic of the Architect’s home city: the hues of sunset over a seaport, the banners that mark a city’s many temples, a city’s soil and the stone from which its structures are quarried. It’s very common for Architect anima banners to include more than just visual displays, often manifesting her city’s sounds and scents.

Anima Effects

An Architect’s anima effects depend on the Foundation Attributes chosen for her city:

• Appearance—Picturesque Vista Embodiment: Once per day, the Architect can add (higher of Essence or 3) non-Charm dice on an influence roll with any Attribute to instill a Tie of lust or attraction toward herself or a to seduce someone with a persuade or bargain roll. If she has Hideous, this applies to threaten rolls instead.

An Architect’s iconic anima banner might be a symbol associated with her home city, an animal native to her home city, prominent aspects of urban life in her home city, or a structure or monument — either real or idealized.

• Charisma—Never a Stranger: The Architect ignores up to (Essence) points of penalties on influence rolls with any Attribute caused by faux pas, unfamiliarity with local customs or group dynamics, or inappropriate clothing or demeanor. She can pay three motes to treat any negative Ties a character has towards foreigners or outsiders that applies to her as one level of intensity lower for a single influence roll.

Architects can spend one mote to perform one of the following effects:

• Manifest a sound or smell associated with their home city, or a phantasmagorical visual display of a symbol associated with it. These are obviously illusory if examined but suffice to confirm the Exigent’s identity as the Architect of her home city to the learned.

### Sorcery and Necromancy

### Martial Arts

Architects are restricted by the Terrestrial keyword (Exalted, p. 427) when using Martial Arts. They’re limited in their ability to combine Martial Arts Charms with their native Charms. When they make a Martial Arts attack, they can enhance it with either Architect Charms or Martial Arts Charms, but not both, with the exception of Excellencies and Versatile Charms. This doesn’t apply to Charms that

EX3

Architects are capable of initiating into Terrestrial Circle sorcery. Architects of cities touched by death, like Sijan, might be able to master Ivory Circle necromancy instead of learning sorcery. Their Intelligence Attribute determines whether they receive the Favored Attribute discount on spells.

### Evocations

At character creation, an Architect’s player chooses one magical material — treating each color of jade as a separate material — or other exotic material that best fits

the Architect’s home city thematically: black jade for a prominent seaport, starmetal for a city of many temples, soulsteel for a city where an ancestor cult is prominent or a shadowland lies nearby, etc. The Architect is neutral with the chosen material and dissonant with all other materials (Arms of the Chosen, p. 16).

### The Great Curse

The Architects’ Great Curse is subtle but insidious, slowly dissolving the boundaries between the Architect and her home city. She experiences thoughts, emotions, and impulses that originate from her city’s nature, or from the goals and ideals of prominent factions within the city or the city father. Unlike Solars and Lunars, Architects don’t have a Limit track or experience Limit Break. While the Great Curse still influences their behavior, its manifestations are determined solely by an Architect’s player.

Roleplaying a manifestation of the Great Curse is rewarded with Architect Experience (p. XX). However, no matter how dire the Great Curse is for the Architect and other characters, it’s never an excuse to ruin other players’ fun at the table. If a dramatic moment caused by the Great Curse isn’t something that the entire group can appreciate, it doesn’t award Architect Experience. Some example manifestations of the Architects’ Great Curse include:

• An Architect taking significant and self-sacrificing risks to defend her home city. • An Architect responding to an insult with lethal force, as would be appropriate by the customs and laws of her home city.

• The Architect of a city ruled by powerful criminal syndicates committing a spree of impulsive crimes that don’t serve her goals and draw unwanted attention. • The Architect of a prominent center of scholarship becoming so lost in the big picture that they fail to notice the material conditions and suffering of others around them.

• An Architect who is despised by a broad swath of her home city’s populace succumbing to despair and irrational self-criticism. • An Architect overindulging in her city father’s preferred vices, to the detriment of her allies and followers.

### Longevity and Death

An Architect’s lifespan is no greater than a mortal’s, but time spent in her home city doesn’t count toward this span. An Architect’s Exaltation does not persist beyond her death.

### New Merits

Architect of a Thousand Schools (0) — Innate

Prerequisite: Architect of a city with a prominent

culture or institution of martial arts or similar ties to martial arts.

The Architect’s battle prowess exemplifies her home city’s martial traditions, drawing from the city’s Essence to transcend her limits. She gains the Martial Artist Merit for free and isn’t limited by the Terrestrial keyword when using Martial Arts Charms. Drawback: The Architect receives one fewer Foundation Attribute from her home city at character creation. She still receives the anima effect for the Attribute she forgoes.

Architect of the Tower Arcane (0) — Innate

Prerequisite: Architect of a city with a prominent culture or institution of sorcery or similar ties to sorcery.

Sorcerous power suffuses the Architect’s home city, tracing out a vast sigil in streets and bridges that the Architect has internalized within her Essence. She automatically gains Terrestrial Circle Sorcery and can learn Terrestrial Circle spells for eight experience points each. She can also initiate into the Celestial Circle of sorcery, learning Celestial spells for ten experience points each. Drawback: The Architect chooses one fewer Foundation Attribute for her home city at character creation. She still receives the anima effect for the Attribute she forgoes.

## Character Advancement

Architects use Terrestrial advancement rules (p. XX).

### Exigent Experience

In addition to experience awarded each session, Architects can earn Exigent experience (p. XX). They receive Expression Bonuses as normal, but don’t

EX3

receive Role Bonuses — instead, they can receive a Foundation Bonus of 2 Exigent experience by: • Intentionally ceding the “spotlight” of a scene’s focus to another player character so that he can express his character concept in an interesting and dramatic fashion, or directly supporting him in such a moment.

Keystone Charms have alternative prerequisite Charms from this second Attribute, unless they have no prerequisite Charms or their prerequisites also have Keystone. This extends to the Attribute minimums of any automatic upgrades or repurchases of the Charm, but not to any dice rolls or other calculations involved. Metropolis: Charms with the Metropolis keyword have an enhanced effect when used within a city or a specific urban environment. Most of the time, it should be obvious whether characters are in a city or not. If there’s any ambiguity, the Storyteller resolves it. The most important criteria in evaluating whether a given location counts as a city are whether they are permanent settlements, whether they are densely populated, and whether they have defined boundaries. These aren’t the only considerations, nor are they absolute rules, but they should be sufficient for resolving most ambiguities.

• Roleplaying the effects of the Great Curse in a way that reveals something about the character, develops her personality, or provides a character moment that everyone at the table enjoys. • Enduring significant peril to protect a city or its city father; creating a lasting and meaningful change to a city; advancing one of the character or her Circle’s goals by inspiring others to uphold the traditions, laws, and customs of a city; resolving a dispute between a city’s populace and a city father or other urban deity; or upholding a Major or Defining Intimacy by engaging with a city’s government, legal system, or similarly prominent institutions or organizations.

### Excellencies

Architects must purchase individual Excellencies for each Attribute, other than the two free Excellencies they receive at character creation. They may add up to (Attribute) dice to rolls, or (Attribute + Essence, maximum 10) in cities. Automatic successes count as two dice towards this limit. Static values such as Evasion or Resolve can be raised by half her dice cap, rounded down. In addition to adding dice to (Attribute + Ability) rolls, the Strength Excellency can add dice to Strength-based withering damage before soak, while the Stamina Excellency can raise soak. This costs one mote per damage die or point of soak, maximum (Attribute/2, rounded down), or ([Attribute + Essence] / 2, rounded down) in cities. These limits only apply to Excellencies, not to other magic that adds damage or soak. Players must declare these Excellencies before rolling.

### New Keywords

Keystone: Keystone Charms can be learned as Charms of alternative Attributes if the Architect has them as Foundation Attributes, using different minimum Attributes and potentially enjoying Keystone discounts.
