EX3

Clear-Eyes Lai woke from fevered nightmares into the safety of his bedroom. Slick with sweat, he took in the familiar opulence, the plaques and trophies commemorating accomplishments of his youth, and thought, What a cruel dream this is. He had traveled the Wyld far, far too long to trust such comfort. Lai threw off his bedding and endured ancient pain to channel Essence into scintillant arms and armor. A woman with gray-flecked hair entered his room, alerted by light and sound, and Lai would have killed her if she hadn’t countered his brilliant spear with her own shimmering shield.

“...Am I home?” Lai asked. “Have I found Uluiru at last, or another Wyld mirage?” In response, the woman slid open a window and let in cold Northern air.

“Welcome home, cousin,” she said. “When I last saw you, I was young and you had sworn to liberate the MountainPiercing Javelin from the Wyld. Now I am older, and you…?” Lai felt the judgment in her question, and the sting of failure. Such casual cruelty was familiar; he truly was home. “I remember your face, Jyu Bird-of-the-Summer, but I don’t recall you as a cousin, let alone a fellow Sovereign.” Jyu sat respectfully but fearlessly at the edge of Lai’s bed. Her face revealed neither pain nor relief as her shield sublimated into shining motes. Only her graying hair betrayed the cost of a Sovereign’s power. “Much has changed,” said she. “Fortunately for you, I take no offense at your attempted assassination. I know how the Wyld blends reality and fantasy. I dragged you, raving, from the bordermarch’s edge myself. You’ve been gone for thirty years, Lai.”

Only that? thought Lai, though he dared not show emotion. Instead, he dismissed his brilliant arms and took a formal sitting position. “My thanks cousin.” He released a breath. “It is true that I haven’t succeeded in my quest… yet. I don’t relish facing Queen Ulu empty-handed, but I feel hale enough, and I’m sure she’s summoned me.” Jyu allowed several moments of silence. “Much has changed.”

“You don’t mean...”

“The queen has been dead just shy of half a year, cousin.”

Lai paled. It was impossible to imagine immortal Queen Ulu’s passing, so he embraced the more familiar suffering of guilt. “I… I should have been here. I could have done something.” “You still can, cousin,” said Jyu, “though Uluiru’s time grows short. We stand upon the edge of chaos, yet no Sovereign yet dares claim the crown.”

“The queen chose no heir?” He shakes his head. “Of course. None were worthy in those days.” Not even myself. “We all want a worthy ruler who can keep the likes of Wise-Eyed Oja and Silken Lua at bay. Swan’s-Grace Thei had the people’s adoration, but she’s paid a steep price for her gentle nature.”

Lai was overwhelmed by three decades of missed history and half-remembered names, but he was a Sovereign of Uluiru, and the court’s movements were in his blood. Jyu had not saved him out of kindness. Though he remembered her as the scion of an unremarkable family, Jyu now exuded ambition. Lai cut to the meat of her budding argument:

“You want me to support your claim to the throne.”

Jyu smiled in satisfaction. “The Wyld hasn’t completely dulled your faculties.” “Nor my ambition,” Lai hazarded, unsure if he spoke truly. “Why should I tie myself to your claim, and not my own?”

“You’ll find the court has changed in your absence. Many of our cousins are complacent and don’t truly understand the Wyld’s threat. They won’t forgive your failures as I might.” Jyu cocked her head. “Harbor your own ambitions if you must, but consider if you wish to face the court with no allies at all.”

As Lai considered his cousin’s argument, he glanced around once more at his childhood room. He felt as trapped as when he’d awoken. What a cruel dream this is, indeed.

# Chapter Eight: The Sovereigns of Uluiru

Chapter Eight

The Sovereigns

of Uluiru

The god-kings of Uluiru blaze with glory. The best and brightest of the royal family bathe in the rainbow flame of dead gods; those who survive its overwhelming power emerge from it Exalted.

The Sovereigns are bright — so terribly, wondrously bright. To look on them is to be blinded with devotion and pride. They weave magic from crystal and auroral light, summoning prismatic armies or binding monsters in a diamond’s facets. They intrigue against one another, jockeying for position — most of all now that the first and greatest of the Sovereigns, Queen Ulu, is dead. More than anything else, they burn: The power inside them is not wicked, but neither is it right. It consumes them if they let it, quickens their worst instincts, transfixes them with ceaseless pain, and turns them into tyrants and torturers.

## History

Sovereigns are born in the dark cradle of the earth, in a cavern below their capital of Uluiru. Three hundred years ago, the gem-god Cantata-of-the-Depths came here with the flame of Exigence cradled in his hands, knowing by myth, rumor, and instinct that this was the barrow-hill of an ancient god felled in the Divine Revolution. In pride and desperation, Cantata mingled his own Essence with the dead god’s imperishable blood; he was consumed in an instant, leaving a pool of liquid fire. This is the Fount of Glories. Until her death, Queen Ulu controlled access to the Fount with icy efficiency, stationing demons, elementals, and crystalline eidolons throughout the caverns. Only members of her royal family are ever permitted access, and even then, only those who prove themselves.

Accordingly, candidates for the Sovereignty have traditionally been raised in an atmosphere of relentless

EX3

one-upmanship — weighed and measured, every success and failure becoming part of the quiet calculus of who’d be allowed the opportunity to Exalt. This demanded, at a minimum, admirable performance in the Forty-Four Distinctions, a grueling series of physical competitions and civil exams. Beyond this, Queen Ulu favored faithful service and bold action, especially in any royal scion brave enough to slay, bargain with, or outwit the Fair Folk.

Not all granted the opportunity to visit the Fount of Glories did so immediately, or even at all. Some who bathed themselves in its Essence were consumed by the flames. Others emerged frail and strange, their shriveled bodies ill-suited for the power they attempted to channel. No consistent pattern has been discerned in who succeeds and who fails, but theory and superstition abound, and each branch of the royal family has its own dubious regime of preparations: The sorcerer Grim-Faced Tanoh subjected himself to dozens of demonic possessions and exorcisms to strengthen his spirit, while forge-master Hwei Burning-Heart engaged in grueling austerities to accustom himself to blinding light and fathomless heat.

While powerful, Sovereigns aren’t immortal — a fact made clear by the death of Queen Ulu’s granddaughter and chosen heir, Nuwa Lyre-Song. Slain by fae assassins, the girl’s death prompted Queen Ulu into a one-woman crusade…a crusade that ended with the queen as dead as her heir. For six months, the Sovereigns have mourned their queen. Ulu has been celebrated and eulogized for weeks on end, her spirit propitiated with countless sacrifices and prayers offered in her name by priests and citizens alike. Her death, so soon after that of her appointed heir, has thrown the Sovereign Host into a time of uncertainty, danger, and ambition, with the succession an open question.

When the proscribed mourning for Queen Ulu finally concludes, power will pass to whoever seizes and

## Cantata-of-the-Depths

## To Reign in Uluiru

holds it best. Already, dozens of schemes are in motion, pieces quietly moving into place across a great gameboard in anticipation of the first big play.

Cantata-ofthe-Depths

Long ago, before he was Cantataof-the-Depths, he was a cavern wisp — a minor god of gems and trickery who led travelers astray when they entered his subterranean domain. The Irugu clan settled at his mountain’s foot, shepherds and farmers who eked out a meager living from the land. Children, brave and foolish, would dare one another to clamber down the dark

and narrow caverns that dotted the mountain in

search of shiny things. Whether by pity, loneliness, or some small spark of paternal pride, the wisp became their

patron, guiding, protecting, and singing for them in his sunless home. In ten generations, he had a new name in their

prayers:

Cantata-ofthe-Depths! Cantataof-the-Depths! Lord of mine and gem, guiding

song and watcher of

ways!

He would not remember until the Irugu were driven from their home by the predations of the raksha Winter Folk. On that long exodus through bitter snow, he found strength in and for his people, bolstering their spirits with song and stretching his own divine power thin to bless them with fortitude and resolve. He became a grandfather to the Irugu, not just a patron, and took their brave queen Ulu as his beloved shortly before unmaking himself in the Fount of Glories.

## Fallen Aurora

The Sovereigns’ other patron, the fallen Incarna Aurora (p. XX), has many titles: Hopebringer, Lord of Delights, the Muse of Seven-Colored Flame. The shimmering curtains of the aurora were his billowing robes, and he danced in the night to remind mortals that the dawn would come again. He was awe, fascination, midnight inspiration — the wondrous insight that blazed brightest in the dark.

That is what the Sovereigns say of him, and it has more in it of aspiration and myth-making than of history. They do not know of his role in the Divine Revolution, or even that he was once counted as

a peer to the Highest of Holies. All that is known is that he is gone, his ichor mixed with Cantata’s own in the creation of the Fount of Glories.

Now bold with praise,

Cantata accepted the

role of patron god of the Irugu, waxing with might and majesty. He anointed kings and queens with diamond dust, showered them in gold and rubies that marked their status as his beloved. He grew regal and vain, forgetting that he had once been nothing more than a tiny flame flickering beneath the earth.

To Reign in

Uluiru

Like a riot of color amidst the far Northwest’s fathomless white, Uluiru stands proudly in an otherwise unhospitable land. It owes its bounty in equal measure to the Sovereigns’ power and its people’s sheer will, for neither could long endure without the other.

EX3

While Exaltation raises a member of the royal family into the ranks of the god-queens, the Sovereigns depend on their positions in Uluiru’s many ministries and provincial governments for political power. Most eagerly seize positions when offered; Queen Ulu doled them out judiciously to prevent any one Exalt from growing too strong, but since her death, control over the various levers of power has fallen into disarray. Those ministries that once fell under Queen Ulu’s direct control must now contend with pressure from all sides, weighing one patron against another all while maintaining the air of neutrality. Other ministries change hands as currency in the game of Sovereign favor-trading, or are taken outright by those Sovereigns who are willing to push their authority over another’s. None of this is legal, but maintaining the thin veneer of legitimacy requires the ministries and their Sovereign overseers to pay at least grudging lip service to the covenants laid down by their lost queen, finding some obscure or ambiguous precedent to justify whatever course they choose.

The Sovereigns represent an extremely formidable power bloc in an otherwise lightly populated region. While they only directly rule Uluiru and its surrounding provinces, they act as a local hegemon whose influence extends south for hundreds of miles until the borders of Fajad. Within this domain, Uluiru is a hub for trade, especially in the wealth of minerals that can be mined from the North’s snow-capped mountains. They export these goods to neighbors to the south and west, bringing back food, medicine, cloth, and other essentials of life.

The Realm has predictably cold relations with the Sovereigns of Uluiru; both sides are far too much alike to develop any real trust. Still, Queen Ulu sent Sovereign envoys to the Imperial City from time to time, usually when the Scarlet Empress or one of her Great Houses had need of their unique talents. How this relationship may change when someone finally claims the empty throne of either the Realm or Uluiru is anyone’s guess.

Further details about Uluiru and its politics can be found in Across the Eight Directions.

## The Fount of Glories

There’s nothing more precious to the Sovereigns and to Uluiru than the Fount of Glories. While most know it only in stories, every Sovereign has bathed in its Essence and emerged Exalted. Unlike other sources

EX3

of Exigent Exaltation, it appears well and truly inexhaustible, having never guttered or dimmed no matter how many Sovereigns emerged from it. Even so, Queen Ulu was never eager to test the limits of her precious miracle.

Even after Exalting, Sovereigns have been known to visit the Fount when they must meet as equals rather than rivals, trusting that none among their number would endanger the very source of their power. Despite three centuries of study, the Fount’s nature remains enigmatic. At the least of its powers, it can serve as a potent Means for sorcerous workings (Exalted, p. 487) and as a source of raw Essence on par with the mightiest demesnes. If a Sovereign could control access to it as Ulu once did, she’d hold the future of Uluiru and the entire Sovereignty in the hollow of her hand.

## Perils of the Wyld

Living so near the edge of the world is a dangerous proposition at the best of times, but Uluiru’s people have a long, bitter history with the Fair Folk and Wyldthings who lurk at their borders. For young Sovereigns (and mortal candidates for the Sovereignty), returning to court with fae war-trophies is a common way of competing for prominence. This is balanced carefully against a need to avoid unnecessarily antagonizing the monsters at their doorstep; while the Sovereign Host might be strong enough to stand against faerie armies, this is never without cost. Some deal peacefully with their raksha neighbors, engaging in a flourishing trade in goblin treasures, studying the esoteric lore of the Fair Folk, or taking fae paramours.

The greatest and most dangerous prize a Sovereign could claim from the Wyld are the heads of Nuwa Lyre-Song’s killers. Anyone able to bring some clarity to Nuwa’s senseless death — and to Queen Ulu’s own passing — would earn tremendous influence and acclaim. The assassins’ identities remain unknown; the following examples are options for the Storyteller to choose from or potentially use as antagonists unrelated to Uluiru. If you include Hearteaters (p. XX) in your game, these optionally canonical Exalted make natural foils to the Sovereigns of Uluiru as the warped, monstrous Chosen of Aurora. The Sovereigns know nothing of their kindred Chosen, most likely presuming them to be unbelievably puissant fae at first. Murdering Nuwa may have been an opening bid to force Queen Ulu into a misstep and leave her city open to infiltration. The Hearteaters’ most likely endgame is seizing the Fount

of Glories, believing they can use it to gain greater power or undo their corruption.

The warbands of the Thousand Talon Clan roam across the Northwest, wielding lances of screaming metal and riding unicorns caparisoned with ribbons of woven lamentation. The nomadic court raids fae and mortals alike, plundering treasure, seizing hostages, and feasting on fear. The clan’s leader, the TalonPierced Queen, is not an individual, but a title that must be passed to another before the season’s end lest its impaling thorns destroy her from within. Besieging Uluiru would be an ordeal even for the Thousand Talon Clan, but the events set in motion by Nuwa’s assassination have weakened the city’s defenses considerably. The Mirror Domain is not one court, but two. Long ago, some wrathful horror of the deep Wyld clove a faerie court from their reflections; within the Mirror Domain’s freehold, each Fair Folk’s reflection is itself a raksha. Fae courtiers scheme with and against their reflections, though it’s not always clear which is which: decades ago, the court of reflections staged a political coup that inverted the Domain, changing places with their originals. The shattered reflection Irael, a prophetic anchorite, presides over the largest of the court’s mercurial cliques; his foremost rivals are the limb-witch Lady Maug and the sagacious ape Wicked Money. If the Mirror Domain had a hand in Nuwa’s assassination, it’s doubtless part of their endless intrigues, with one clique seeking to play Uluiru against the others.

more intimate in scale. It’s all but certain that every Sovereign knows each and every one of her peers, and while the royal family has many branches, they’re just that — branches of one family, far smaller than even the smallest of the Great Houses but no less proud or complex. When the Sovereigns contend for the throne, it’s not against cousins six-times removed, but against brothers and sisters, uncles and aunts, parents and children.

Sovereigns can do well in mixed games as well; their overall strength make them a good fit for playing with Dragon-Blooded. Playing up the similarities and contrasts between these two types of Exalt can help to emphasize the many ways in which family, duty, and pride can manifest. They’re also particularly apt in mixed-Exigent games: As a rare state openly ruled by Exigents, Uluiru may serve as a sanctuary for other Exigents, especially those who might serve as useful allies, agents, and catspaws.

In games with Solars, Lunars, and other Exalted subject to Realm propaganda, Sovereigns can be more difficult to integrate. They lack the raw power of Solars and Lunars, and their most powerful Charms often depend on flaring their animas, announcing their presence for miles around. While Sovereigns can distinguish themselves in many roles as crafters, performers, socialites, and lieutenants, they cannot compete directly with Solars in the same areas of expertise — at least not without approaching the issue laterally rather than head-on.

Mist, the Eternal Revolutionary (Exalted, p. 502) is an adversary to all rulers. Murdering the heir to the throne may simply be yet another bloody deed in his unceasing pursuit of his Wyld-warped ambitions, or it might have been part of a larger scheme to depose Queen Ulu. Killing the eldest Sovereign in battle is likely beyond Mist’s personal puissance; it’s possible he’s allied with faerie courts or other powers of the Wyld. With the current power vacuum in Uluiru, Mist is left without anyone to oppose, but a Sovereign who succeeds in claiming the throne may find herself faced with a powerful enemy.

### EXIGENT ASPECTS

Unlike other Exalted, Sovereign Aspects don’t have unique Abilities associated with them; all of them share the five Sovereign Abilities. We recommend doing the same if you’re creating Castes or Aspects for an Exigent that only has Charms for a limited selection of Abilities or Attributes (p. XX). Glory, acclaim, and applause soothe their warped, patchwork Essence, while creative struggles or failures exacerbate it, eroding their self-confidence and leaving them overly dependent on others. Anima Powers

Beloved By All the World: While the Sovereign’s anima is at glowing or higher, other characters must pay one Willpower to initiate hostilities against her and her companions, unless provoked by their actions or words. Once a character resists, he’s immune for the rest of the day.

Crystalline Cynosure Radiance: For five motes, the Sovereign adds a non-Charm success on rolls against characters with Resolve lower than her Appearance until her next turn. This is free at bonfire anima or above.

Inspiring Grandeur: For three motes, add (Anima) non-Charm dice on an influence roll involving awe, reverence, or wonder, or that leverages Intimacies based on those emotions.

Exigent Experience

Once per session, Sapphire Aspects earn 2 Exigent XP when they:

• Advance their or their Circle’s goals through artistry, craftsmanship, or seduction.

Their iconic animas might display a towering crystal giant that reflects her self-image, a rain or precious gemstones or a ferocious blizzard of sharp-edged diamonds, a garda bird with wings of seven-colored flame, an extravagant palace, a whirlwind of fireglass blades, a shrike overseeing a field of crystal thorns, a dragon with gemstone scales, or the like. Sovereigns often derive their personal heraldry from their anima’s colors and iconic display. Sovereigns with Fount-of-Glories Incarnation (p. XX) are capable of reaching a level beyond bonfire: transcendent anima. In addition to the Aspect anima powers listed above, Sovereigns can spend one mote to do one of the following:

• Create a small decorative or ornamental object of fireglass (p. XX) — elegant utensils, jeweled decorations, glowing gemstones — that lasts until the scene ends. They’re ill-suited to practical use; relying on these constructs as equipment imposes a penalty that’s only one less than the penalty for using no equipment at all. • Sense the direction and approximate distance of the Fount of Glories.

### Martial Arts

Sovereigns are restricted by the Terrestrial keyword (Exalted, p. 427) when using Martial Arts. They’re limited in their ability to combine Martial Arts Charms with their native Charms. When they make a Martial Arts attack, they can enhance it with either Sovereign Charms or Martial Arts Charms, but not both, with the exception of Excellencies and Versatile Charms (p. XX). This doesn’t apply to Charms that are permanent or provide ongoing benefits, nor to actions other than attacking.

### Sorcery

• Cause a narratively significant character to form a positive Major or Defining Tie toward them.

Sovereigns can initiate into Terrestrial Circle sorcery or Ivory Circle necromancy, but not both. Their Occult Ability determines whether they receive the Favored Ability discount on spells.

• Create a lasting and meaningful work of beauty. • Uphold a Major or Defining Intimacy with the aid of a patron, admirer, or similar backer, or that of their subordinates (p XX).

### Evocations

### Anima

A Sovereign’s anima banner encompass the colors of the aurora, predominated by the gemstone hues of her Aspect.

EX3

Sovereigns are neutral with adamant and dissonant with all other materials. They can develop resonance with adamant using Adamant Perfection Attainment (p. XX).

### MIRACLES OF ADAMANT

Adamant is to diamond as orichalcum is to gold: superior not just in strength, but in spiritual majesty. Lodes of adamant are most often found in the distant North and South, born of extreme temperatures, isolation, and stillness. Even in the rough, it has shine and luster to match a masterfully cut diamond. Most artificers grind it to dust and alloy it with steel, much like jade; knapping and carving it often produces superior designs but requires rare tools and expertise.

### The Great Curse

The Great Curse smolders within the Sovereigns, a baleful flame that burns along the seams of their patchwork Exigence. If their will falters, if the stress becomes too much to bear, it will consume them from within, an agonizing torment that drives them to acts of cruelty and self-destruction.

Sovereigns’ Great Curse manifests through a ten-point Limit Track (p. XX). They roll dice and gain Limit equal to their successes under the following circumstances. • Once per scene, when a Sovereign acts against a Major Intimacy, she rolls one die (unless she’s already rolled for acting against a Defining Intimacy). Voluntarily weakening an Intimacy or spending Willpower to resist influence it supports counts as acting against it.

Rare compared even to the other magical materials and beyond the power of most Exalted to fully resonate with, adamant is uncommonly used in artifice, though it could be numbered as the sixth of the five magical materials.

Adamant is associated with clarity, precision, keen senses, and graceful action. Its Essence is unyielding, timeless, and eternal. Adamant artifacts magnify, reflect, and refract, enhancing or distorting traits like light split through a prism. It’s also associated with sharpness, fascination, illusion, scrying, logic, order, protection, and extremes temperatures — the heat of focused light and the crystalline luster of ice.

• Once per scene, when a Sovereign acts against a Defining Intimacy, she rolls two dice (or one die, if she’s already rolled for acting against a Major Intimacy).

• When a Sovereign allows a challenge to go unanswered or submits to another character’s authority, she rolls three dice. She doesn’t gain Limit for submitting to characters for whom she has a positive Major or Defining Tie or to other Sovereigns.

Sample adamant artifacts include:

Diamond-Fire Ratha, a war chariot that crosses unimpeded through snow and ice, its crystalline wheels burning with colorless flame. Elegant Snowfall Awning, a razor parasol that can fend off any attack with paramount grace and unshakable fortitude. The Empty-Heart Yumi, a powerbow whose wielder may purge their emotions and irrational thoughts as arrows of heat and cold. The Eon Mantle, a suit of articulated plate that holds back the travails of time, preserving its wearer against age, wounds, and pestilence. Facet Razor, a reaper daiklave whose blade is infinitely sharp, said to be capable of cutting through anything in the hands of one who’s mastered it. Sevenfold Harmony, an adamant harp, whose seven strings each have a unique mesmeric power when strummed.

Sovereigns lose one Limit for accomplishing a legendary social goal (Exalted, p. 134). Additionally, they lose one Limit for forcing a powerful and narratively relevant enemy or rival to submit to their authority.

When a Sovereign reaches Limit 10, she blazes with white-hot Essence as her soul begins to immolate itself, either immediately or at a suitably dramatic moment. The Sovereign chooses which of the following Limit Breaks she enters, either suffering the overwhelming pain of Agony Cataclysmic and lashing out at those around her or steeling herself in the Diamond Heart Trance by suppressing emotion and empathy. Agony Cataclysmic

The Sovereign’s body cracks and blisters, revealing not flesh inside of her, but fiery anima. She is overwhelmed by pain; her wound penalty is −4 unless it would normally be higher. Driven by this pain, she lashes out, physically or emotionally, at anyone and everyone at hand. She can refrain from physically harming characters for whom

EX3

she has positive Ties. When her anima banner flares, it sloughs off waves of molten glass; at the start of each of her turns, she rolls (Anima) dice of withering damage against all characters within close range, friend or foe. She doesn’t gain Initiative from this. Crashed characters suffer lethal decisive damage instead.

Duration: Scene. This ends if the Sovereign sees how

her actions have caused someone for whom she has a positive Major or Defining Tie to fear or reject her. Diamond Heart Trance

The Sovereign cages the roaring flame within her through sheer will, her heart growing cold as crystal as she numbs herself to passion as well as pain. Her emotion-based Intimacies are suppressed, as if she didn’t have them, and she can’t voluntarily form new ones. She is neither willing nor able to consider the emotions of others; while she need not be malicious, she cares not whom she enrages, terrifies, or drives to despair in pursuit of her goals.

Duration: Session. This ends if a character to whom

she has a positive Tie (suppressed or not) shows her how her actions have harmed one of her suppressed Major or Defining Intimacies.

### Longevity and Death

Sovereigns live for centuries, although their full lifespans remain uncertain. They begin to show signs of aging sooner than other Exalted, though not as soon as mortals —their unstable, patchwork Exigence burns away their youth before their years. Like the Dragon-Blooded, a Sovereign’s Exaltation is snuffed out when they perish, but the Fount of Glories itself seems inexhaustible.

## Character Advancement

Sovereigns use Terrestrial advancement rules (p. XX). They receive Exigent Experience from Expression Bonuses as usual and can earn Aspect Bonuses for satisfying the criteria listed for their Aspect. Aspect bonuses can also be earned by ceding the “spotlight” of a scene’s focus to another player’s character to enable a dramatic moment that supports his character concept, or directly supporting him in such a moment.

## Charms

Sovereign Charms reflect both Cantata-of-the-Depths’ past as trickster, savior, and tutelary god of the mines and Aurora’s awe-inspiring beauty. They only have

EX3

Charms for Craft, Integrity, Performance, Socialize, and War, though their Charms encompass the full range of Exalted competency.

### Excellencies

Sovereigns have Excellencies for all twenty-five Abilities. They must purchase individual Excellencies for each Ability, other than the five free Excellencies they receive at character creation.

Sovereigns may add up to (4 + Anima) dice to rolls. Automatic successes count as two dice towards this limit. Static values such as Evasion or Resolve can be raised by half her dice limit, rounded down. An action’s dice limit is determined before paying any anima costs for Charms that enhance it.

### Charm Concept: Fireglass

Many Sovereign Charms create things out of fireglass, crystalline light that shines with the colors of a Sovereign’s anima. Fireglass is incredibly resilient and grows only stronger as a Sovereign’s Essence increases. The Strength minimum and difficulty needed to destroy a Sovereign’s fireglass depend on her Essence, as follows:

Essence

1-2

3-4

5+

Strength Minimum

Difficulty

5-9

10-14

15-20

A character familiar with a Sovereign’s anima banner can recognize her fireglass as her handiwork with a difficulty 3 (Perception + Occult) roll. Upon a Sovereign’s death, her fireglass shatters.

### Charm Concept: Subordinates

Sovereigns are born to rule; their Charms hold especial power over those who serve them. Subordinates include characters over whom a Sovereign holds legitimate authority within an organization or culture group (often represented by Backing). It also includes characters in her debt, either financially or socially, or characters currently deferring to her authority or expertise, like evacuees following her directions, though this status ends once the debt is repaid or the character stops following the Sovereign’s directive for a scene. Storyteller characters attached to the Sovereign

through the Command, Cult, Followers, Retainers, or similar Merits are always subordinates unless story events cause the Sovereign to lose the respective Merit.

### CRAFT CHARMS

Sovereign Craft Charms draw on Cantata’s themes of crystal, wealth, and exchange, especially in creating and distributing tribute. They also resonate with Cantata’s own journey from minor god to major, allowing the Sovereigns to create and uplift eidolons of their own making. Finally, Craft is a repository for complex aurora-shaping magic that demonstrate the Sovereign’s growing creative prowess.

### Performance

#### Prismatic Phantasmagoria

Cost: 1m; Mins: Performance 1, Essence 1

Type: Supplemental

Keywords: None

Duration: One performance

Prerequisite Charms: None

### PERFORMANCE CHARMS

Sovereign Performance Charms are firmly rooted in Aurora’s role as a muse, and Cantata’s origin as a wandering cavern-wisp and trickster. These Charms are about inspiring awe and gathering followers (sometimes literally), whether to protect them and deliver them safely through their trials or to lead them astray.

The Sovereign’s virtuoso spirit overflows from her performance as auroral imagery, expressing her most profound passions.

The Sovereign can create illusions from heatless flame in the colors of her anima as part of a performance, letting her ignore multiple target penalties. They can extend out to short range from her; individual illusions can be up to the size of a person. Onlookers can be convinced that these illusions are real with social influence — potentially the Performance roll enhanced by this Charm — but otherwise won’t be deceived by them.

With Performance 5, Essence 3, the Sovereign can create larger illusions, up to Legendary Size.

### Socialize

#### Imperious Command

### SOCIALIZE CHARMS

Sovereign Socialize Charms are the truest blend of their many themes, with a focus on subordinate-superior relationships and reciprocity. These are the Charms that give them their name and empower them as the god-kings of Uluiru. They’re also the Charms that draw most on Cantata’s life as a power broker and patron god of mines and the wealth of the earth.

### COSTS AND CALCULATIONS

When you use a Charm with an anima cost together with a Charm that uses your current anima as part of a calculation or that gains additional effects based on your anima — like using Arcing Rainbow Slash together with Heavenly Fire Sheath — you use your anima’s level after paying the cost to determine those effects, unless otherwise specified. The same is true for other resources, like temporary Willpower and Initiative. A Sovereigns’ dice limit is a notable exception; levels of anima spent on an action still are still counted toward the cap.

With a wave of her hand, the Sovereign raises a bulwark of fireglass.

The Sovereign can use this Charm on her turn to create a fireglass barrier that provides light cover (Exalted, pp. 199). She adds (higher of Essence or 3) dice on rolls to take cover behind it that scene. The barrier is permanent; any character can take cover behind it. With a War 5, Essence 3 repurchase, this Charm creates heavy cover. At bonfire anima or higher, the Sovereign may pay a five-Initiative, one-Willpower surcharge to surround herself in a sphere of crystal, providing full cover without the need for a take cover

action. She must spend five Initiative at the start of

each subsequent turn to sustain this barrier or it cracks and weakens to heavy cover. The same occurs if her anima drops below bonfire.

Special activation rules: This Charm may be flurried. If the Sovereign flurries it with a take cover action, she ignores the flurry penalty and her Defense isn’t penalized.

Nyla’s corpse lay a hundred miles away, a banquet for the raitons.

Her last moments stayed with her, one more death in a long chain spanning all the way back to the war at the dawn of history and the unthinkable betrayal that followed. This most recent death came at the hands of Darim Crimson-Clawed. The triumph in the Lunar’s eyes seared itself into Nyla’s memory as their wicked claws tore open her throat. And they knew how to kill a Hearteater, had found the pawns she’d made vessels for her will and killed them, too.

Most of them, but not all.

Nyla’s final pawn blazed with the fires of Exaltation, but it was not he who would emerge Chosen. The Hearteater had broken his will long ago; it was no hard thing to overcome his consciousness, to devour it whole and claim this body for herself once and forevermore. She opened new eyes, their vision a little weaker than her last, though rapidly correcting as Essence suffused her flesh. She felt the last creak this body’s bones would ever make and the ache flowing out of work-wearied muscle. She took in her surroundings and smiled. Exactly where she wanted to be — sitting at Darim’s campfire. The Lunar had created a promising young dominion here in the wilderness, far enough from the satrapies for the Realm to pose little threat to it. Darim was a student of the Silver Pact’s greatest generals and a veteran of the Caul; now he had returned to his home to teach his people his ideology and lead them to triumph. “Grandfather.” A youth crouched before the fire at Nyla’s side. He was no kin to her new body — hardly anyone in the camp was — but it was how they’d all addressed her. Her pawn had been with Darim Crimson-Clawed from the start; part of his inner circle. The dominion’s people sought out his advice, heeded his counsel, and followed his orders. The young man passed her a sealed note on heavy vellum. “A rider brought this.”

Nyla held his gaze as she took the letter. She already knew him — Keral, a warrior’s name. Her pawn’s mind was extinguished, but something of his passions and memories lingered on. She knew that Keral often talked with the old man for hours on end, that the youth burned with desire to earn Darim’s respect and march in their vanguard. “Walk me to Darim’s pavilion,” she said, slipping her arm through his, “and tell me how your patrol went today.”

Keral’s eyes lit up and he held his head high. An unfamiliar part of Nyla delighted in this, but an old man’s fondness wouldn’t save him from a Hearteater’s hunger. Keral cared so deeply for the man whose skin she wore; reaching inside his mind and making him hers was almost too easy. Inside the tent, Darim and their advisors pored over the latest reports. Darim’s wife, a solidly-built woman resting her hand on a sword’s pommel, made room for Nyla at the table. Darim smiled fondly as Nyla took her place. “Grandfather.” They said it as more than simply an endearment. Darim’s face resembled the pawn’s in the curve of their cheek and the tilt of their smile. She was their father’s father.

“Grandson.” She passed him the letter. “We’ve had word from the lamp-priests. A rider awaits your reply.” She didn’t bother craning her neck as Darim broke the seal; they would tell her what was inside. Instead, she caught Iskele’s eye. “I can tell you haven’t been sleeping. Come see me tonight,” Nyla said with a stolen voice. “I have a tea that will help you rest.”

Nyla looked around the tent at Darim’s trusted advisors and smiled. Soon enough, every person Darim Crimson-Clawed loved would be gone, every one of their faces now the face of his enemy.

EX3

# Appendix: Creating New Exalted

Appendix

Creating

New Exalted

From a purely design-oriented perspective, there’s little difference between designing an Exigent and designing an entirely new type of Exalt. The main difference is in how they fit into Exalted’s setting. Some Exalted have had had world-shaking impacts on the setting: the Dragon-Blooded of the Scarlet Dynasty, the Lunars of the Silver Pact, the Sidereals of the Bureau of Destiny. Others are subtler presence. The Solars, while massively impactful in the First Age, have been absent from Creation for centuries, only recently returned alongside the corrupted Abyssals and Infernals. Liminals are solitary figures, shunning mortals who would judge them as monsters. Getimians strive to avoid Heaven’s eye as they prosecute their shadow war against it. The Alchemicals dwell within their creator’s world-body, save for a handful created in the Divine Revolution and left in stasis for millennia. The alien Spoken are extinct, slain in the Niobraran War, and their civilization faded into memory.

When adding new Exalted, consider the impact they’ve had on the setting. If you want to use them without significantly deviating from canonical depictions of Creation, think about why they haven’t had a major impact on the setting: perhaps they’ve only recently been created, or they’re very few in number.

If you want your new Exalted to have had a major impact on Creation’s history, you should discuss this with the playgroup to make sure everyone’s on board. You’ll also want to talk with them when it comes to deciding how to handle setting information from the books that’s contradicted by this change. This Appendix presents three new Exalted who are “optional canon,” for Storytellers to include or leave out of their games as they see fit: the Dream-Souled, illusionists and idealists; the Hearteaters, mind-eating horrors; and the Umbrals, tormented by their inner darkness. It doesn’t provide everything needed to play one, but enough of their concept, details, and Charms to give you a start in creating them or to provide inspiration for other new Exalted.

## The Dream-Souled

A merchant nods off in her market stall, dreaming of silver boughs heavy with jade blossoms. An exhausted laborer finds no respite from work in his sleep, building towers that stretch into the clouds and beyond. A priestess drifts in and out of a trance as she respires subterranean vapors, seeing a world where all share her transcendent vision.

### AN APOCRYPHAL CENSUS

As this Appendix’s Exalted are non-canonical, no hard numbers for how many exist in the setting are given. If a Storyteller wishes to include one or more of them in her game, she should determine how many exist. The following guidelines provide a good range within which Storytellers can determine how many or how few of these Exalted they want in their game. Hearteaters: Around 200 to 400 Exaltations total, of which around 0 to 20 are typically active at any given time. Umbrals: Around 50 to 200.

Dream-Souled: Varies; at present, around 25 to 100.

EX3

It is from such sleepers as these that the mysterious Ketu chooses his Dream-Souled, those consumed by a vision of the world as it could be. They wield unmatched power over dreams but are formidable forces in the waking world as well, masters of illusion and transformation. They bend Creation and the Wyld both to their vision, imposing their personal utopia on reality.

The Dream-Souled are newcomers to Creation compared to the likes of the Dragon-Blooded but have nonetheless left their mark on the world. Along the Blessed Isle’s Wandering River, Ophris Kotoba, hero of countless tall tales, is reborn — or rather, a Dynast’s servant has donned Kotaba’s mantle to conceal her true nature as she bedevils the wicked and the hypocritical. The merchant prince Heron of Zebremani seeks lost Cozen, a mythical city born of dreams that turned to nightmare, not realizing that the ruins and relics he finds are forged by his own will. Araya, a scroll-keeper of the legendary Library of Marita, has quietly amassed a trove of tomes and codices thought lost to the ages, and some that were never written at all.

### Ketu, the Dreaming Prince

Ill-known is Ketu, that numinous poet-king who dwells beyond the deep Wyld’s farthest horizons. Neither fae nor god nor kin to the Yozis, the Dreaming Prince has been encountered only rarely even by the deep Wyld’s raksha. In each account, it takes a different form: a gigantic seven-eyed stag whose antlers are coiled around with rainbows; a hungry murmuration of countless birds flying together in the shape of one vast hawk; a beautiful youth whose head has been cleanly severed. Closer to Creation’s edge, the Fair Folk know Ketu only as a name that chills even their hollow hearts, if at all. Almost none in Creation know of the Dreaming Prince — including its Chosen.

Yet distant as Ketu may be from Creation, there is something of the world that intrigues it. It bears witness to all Creation’s dreams — those of mortals, of animals, and of stranger things. Its understanding of Creation, drawn solely from dreams, is fundamentally warped. Its motives are unknown and may be incomprehensible. But it looks into a Creation it does not

EX3

understand and it sees in some rare dreamers a potential to reshape the world. Ketu breathes its divine fire into these sleepers, and they awaken as its Chosen, the Dream-Souled.

The first recorded Dream-Souled arose hundreds of years after the Great Contagion. Perhaps it took that long for Ketu to glean the secret of Exaltation from the dreams of the Chosen; perhaps Ketu discovered the secret through some great and unknown quest; perhaps it simply had not noticed Creation before then.

Ideals

Each Dream-Souled possesses an Ideal: a Defining Principle that reflects her vision or understanding of a perfect world, of what both Creation and the Wyld should be or become. The Ideal can’t be weakened, eroded, or otherwise subverted, either by social influence or the Dream-Souled’s own conscious actions. Example Ideals include:

• No one should have to suffer.

• I should rule over the world.

The Dream-Souled do not know their patron. They receive no prophetic visions or knowledge of Ketu upon their Exaltation, nothing to suggest the existence of some alien and infinitely distant patron. The Dream-Souled are dedicated to their personal Ideals, and few have any need for divine counsel even if they knew to seek it.

• People should be loyal, moral, and scrupulous. • Art should be the highest cause.

• The wise should hold authority over the ignorant.

### Dream-Souled and Other Exalted

Both latecomers among the Chosen and few in number, the Dream-Souled remain an open question to most other Exalted. Most know them only from sporadic interactions with individual Dreamers, whether as allies or enemies — assuming they don’t mistake them for Exigents or puissant Fae-Blooded. The Sidereal Exalted keep well-apprised of the Dream-Souled, counting them as a threat to fate, albeit one that may take decades to come to fruition as they slowly warp the boundaries between Creation and the Wyld. In a perfect world, the Bureau of Destiny would act immediately to thwart their threat, but faced with the more immediate threat of the Getimians, the returned Solars, and the other upheavals of the Time of Tumult, the Bureau can’t afford to devote its limited personnel and resources to the Dreamers. It’s not unthinkable that the Bureau might even sanction a joint operation between Sidereals and Dream-Souled if it served Heaven’s agenda.

The Fair Folk and other fae hate and fear the DreamSouled, recognizing them as a force antithetical to the Wyld as it is now. Unlike the Sidereals, the fae have little reason to stay their hand — while a Dream-Souled traveling through the Wyld need not fear ambush around every corner, she’d be well-advised to conceal her true nature from any fae she encounters.

At the Storyteller’s discretion, a Dream-Souled’s Ideal may change under suitably dramatic circumstances, with the Dream-Souled’s player designating one of her other Defining Principles as their new Ideal. Anima

A Dream-Souled’s anima burns with too-vivid colors, sometimes shifting with the Exalt’s mood. As her anima flares, her dreams begin to spill out into it, filling it with impossible visions. A Dream-Souled’s iconic anima is most often an impossible creature or form that rises up from this surging tide of dream: many-headed chimerical beasts, mind-warping geometrical forms, nightmarish horrors, a whirlwind filled with flowers, etc. Dream-Souled can spend one mote to perform one of the following effects:

• Sense the direction and approximate distance to the nearest pathway into or out of the Wyld within one mile.

• Send a willing character into a deep, dreamful sleep.

### Traits

Anima Effects

Dream Fades Away: For five motes, the Dream-Souled becomes momentarily ephemeral, adding (Essence) non-Charm dice to an attempt to escape confinement, oppose a rush or grapple control roll, or disengage from an attacker. This power is free at bonfire anima.

Dream-Souled are intended for Terrestrial play (p. XX).

Dreamwalker: For ten motes, the Dream-Souled touches a sleeping character to enter his dreams,

EX3

The Great Curse

The Dream-Souled’s Great Curse drives them to obsession, delusion, or fanaticism centered on their Ideal. They have a Limit track and experience Limit Breaks (p. XX). Like most Exalted, they gain Limit from violating Major and Defining Intimacies; any Limit gained from violating their Ideal is doubled. They have a shared Limit Trigger, gaining Limit when their Ideal is challenged, mocked, or threatened.

### SLEEP AND GUILE

The −2 Guile penalty for characters unaware of their observers applies to sleeping characters. Magic like Surprise Anticipation Method (Exalted, p. 267) that lets a character use their senses normally lets sleeping characters perceive the observer’s presence with a successful Awareness roll, negating this penalty.

Concepts for Dream-Souled Limit Breaks include:

rolling ([Charisma, Manipulation, or Wits] + [Occult or Presence]) against his Guile. Within the dream, she is a formless, imperceptible presence incapable of interacting with the sleeper, but she can still attempt to glean insight from his dreams with a special read intentions roll, gaining a useful piece of information on a success: an Intimacy, a glimpse into a memory, a clue relevant to an ongoing mystery, etc. She can only do so once per use of this anima effect, no matter how long she watches her target’s dreams for.

Sculptor of Figments: For three motes, the DreamSouled can create a phantasmal image no larger than a person within short range or similar illusionary phenomena. These phantoms are obviously illusory to any sense and can’t block a character’s line of sight or otherwise impede their senses, but are exceptional equipment (Exalted, p. 580) for influence rolls in which the Dream-Souled uses them to emphasize her words. Illusions vanish at the end of the scene. Martial Arts

Dream-Souled are restricted by the Terrestrial keyword (Exalted, p. 427) when using Martial Arts. They’re limited in their ability to combine Martial Arts Charms with their native Charms. When they make a Martial Arts attack, they can enhance it with either native Charms or Martial Arts Charms, but not both, with the exception of Excellencies. This doesn’t apply to Charms that are permanent or provide ongoing benefits, nor to actions other than attacking. Sorcery

Dream-Souled can initiate into Terrestrial Circle sorcery. Those with bleak Ideals can sometimes initiate into Ivory Circle necromancy, but such Dream-Souled can’t learn sorcery.

Evocations

The Dream-Souled are neutral with moonsilver (Arms of the Chosen, p. 16). They are dissonant with all other materials.

Chimerical Daydream Utopia: The Dream-Souled perceives the world as if her Ideal were reality. She rationalizes away discrepancies and will lash out at those who seek to dissuade her.

Future-Forging Zeal: The Dream-Souled will go to any lengths to make her Ideal a reality, including violence, breaking laws and customs, and helping people against their will.

Incomprehensible Other Affliction: The DreamSouled loses all empathy for those who don’t share her Ideal. She need not be cruel, but she neither understands nor concerns herself with their desires. She’s likewise alienated from communities that don’t share her Ideal, feeling estranged, out of place, and unwelcome.

Universal Meaning Apophenia: The Dream-Souled sees everything as being somehow related to her Ideal. She must prioritize courses of action that address this connection above all others.

Longevity and Death

The Dream-Souled can live for a few centuries. Their Exaltation does not reincarnate after their death; instead, it reunites with distant Ketu, imparting something of the slain Dream-Souled’s vision unto the Dreaming Prince.

## Dream-Souled Charms

Dream-Souled are masters of illusion, transformation, and dreams, wielding these powers to make their Ideal a reality. Their Charms evoke dream-logic, making reality a fluid and malleable thing. The Wyld and its denizens are especially susceptible to the terrifying power of a Dream-Souled’s vision, while Creation is blighted with chaos in their wake.

### Excellencies

Dream-Souled have Excellencies for all Abilities; they receive five for free at character creation and

EX3

must purchase others separately. They may add up to (Ability) dice to rolls, or (Ability + Essence, maximum 10) for actions that uphold their Ideal, paying one mote per die. Automatic successes count as two dice towards this limit. Static values such as Evasion or Resolve can be raised by half this dice cap, rounded down.

Cost: 10m, 2wp; Mins: Essence 3

The Dream-Souled reshapes the terrain within medium range, altering and unmaking natural features as she wishes: she could freeze over a river, turn a copse of trees into a rock formation, raise a hill up from the earth, or transform a tenement into an amphitheater. The Storyteller may require a ([Intelligence or Wits]) + (Craft, Lore, or Occult) roll at difficulty 3+ to create natural features that are complicated or especially advantageous, such as shaping a masterwork of sculpture from a boulder or creating a lode of silver. The Dream-Souled can’t use this Charm if a nontrivial character within medium range is opposed to her doing so — her will must be unquestioned. Within Creation, the transformed area also becomes a bordermarch of the Wyld, posing the risk of mutation and addiction to long-term inhabitants. In the Wyld, she instead shapes the region into an islet of Creation. Other realms of existence may undergo similar changes at the Storyteller’s discretion. The Dream-Souled must maintain her commitment to this Charm for a week to make her transformation permanent. If she ends it prematurely, the transformed terrain and anything taken from it reverts to its original form. Parts of Creation turned to bordermarches revert back, as do parts of the Wyld turned to Creation. Once a week passes, the transformation becomes permanent. Shaped bordermarches will eventually revert back to Creation unless they’re near the Wyld’s edge or somewhere else where reality is weak. The length of time a bordermarch persists increases the further it is created from Creation’s omphalos, the Imperial Mountain: a bordermarch in the far reaches of a Direction can last for years, if not indefinitely; further into the Threshold, they last days or weeks; on the Blessed Isle, they dissipate within hours. Likewise, islets of Creation eventually dissolve back into chaos, lasting longer the further they are from the deep Wyld and the more they interact with things of Creation.

## The Hearteaters

A starving refugee fleeing through the Wyld finds a strange reliquary from another age, filled with pearlescent bones. She can hear them singing to her as she approaches, calling out alone, alone, alone. She touches them, and she is Exalted. For a fleeting instant, the aurora sings inside her soul, filling every part of her being with glory and inspiration. But then the song turns to a scream as the thing that dwelt within the bones batters her senses, seeking to devour her mind and steal her body. Her will to survive is fierce, fiercer than the ancient monster in her soul, and it is she who devours the beast. But there is no feeling of triumph in this. Now she is the monster, and she is so terribly alone.

### The Death of Aurora

Counted as the most beautiful among the Celestial Incarnae (p. XX), Aurora ruled over the lights that bear his name. Artistic, passionate, and gentle, Aurora nonetheless joined in his siblings’ Divine Revolution. His Chosen, the Aurorals, were muses, teachers, and spiritual guides, strengthening the morale and protecting the hearts of the Exalted’s forces.

Then the enemies of the gods murdered Aurora and, upon his still-beating heart, cursed his Chosen, inverting their Exaltation’s nature and twisting them into the Hearteaters, monstrous Exalted with the power to break minds and make willing pawns of their victims. But to the ancients’ dismay, their curse did not turn the Hearteaters against their allies; Aurora’s orphans continued to fight alongside their fellow Chosen, satisfying their monstrous appetites upon the enemies of the gods.

As the First Age dawned amidst the Divine Revolution’s aftermath, the Hearteaters troubled the other Exalted. They had little place in a peaceful realm without a great enemy to direct their hunger against. Some struggled to find a place for themselves — assassins hunting down the Realm’s foes and claiming them as pawns, guardians battling inhuman horrors at the world’s edge, cult leaders recruiting willing disciples to sate their hunger. But in time, the other Exalted betrayed the Hearteaters, murdering their pawns to prevent their Exaltations from reincarnating and sealing their imperishable bones away in prisons deep within the Wyld.

EX3

### HUNGRY MENTORS

Occasionally, the hungry ghost (Exalted, p. 503) of a Hearteater’s previous incarnation remains tethered to its pearlescent bones, waiting for a successor to find the Exaltation caged within. This inhuman revenant may act as a mentor, whether following the new Hearteater or lingering as an oracle in its tomb. Much more powerful than a mortal’s hungry ghosts, they are three-dot Allies or two-dot Mentors.

For much of the First Age, these great prisons held, and the might of the Old Realm smote down any Hearteater who escaped them. When history repeated itself in the Usurpation, the death of the Solars diminished and warped the greatest of the magics that sealed the Hearteaters away. The great invasion of the Fair Folk sundered the last remaining bindings on many of these prisons entirely, opening the way for any mortal foolish enough to wander into the Wyld to free a Hearteater’s Exaltation.

### Starving and Alone

While the Aurorals strove to uplift and inspire others, the Hearteaters’ corruption has warped this into a bone-deep hunger for reverence and acclaim; a desperate need to be seen, to be heard, to be loved or hated; to not be alone. But no audience’s applause, no words of praise, no lover’s embrace can ease this all-consuming need for long. She must prey upon others, breaking their mind and devouring their will until nothing is left but a loyal pawn, an extension of herself. Seeing herself through her pawn’s eyes, she knows that he loves and reveres her, for she gives him no other choice, and for a time, her hunger is sated.

Claiming a pawn demands persistence and dedication. A Hearteater must ensnare her prey’s heart, stirring his passions for her — be they love, hate, or fear — to open his soul to her. A Hearteater’s first pawn is often one of those closest to them, one whose emotional ties to her make them easy prey: a trusted traveling companion, an old friend, a lover, a child. Young Hearteaters can only prey on mortals of weak will, but as they grow in experience and power, they can break the strongest minds and bind beasts, gods, and stranger things. A pawn’s mind remains intact and conscious, retaining that portion of his free will that the Hearteater permits him. When needs must, a Hearteater may step into her pawn’s body, seizing absolute and unquestionable control over him; all he can do is watch from the back of his mind as she commits atrocities with his stolen hands.

Some Hearteaters, especially the newly Exalted, delude themselves, believing their pawns serve them freely out of genuine loyalty, that when they usurp a pawn’s body it is because he permits them. This pleasant lie lets them live with themselves, but it cannot last. In time, every Hearteater confronts the truth of what they’ve become and what they’ve done. Some give in to despair, surrendering to their monstrous hunger. Others struggle against their nature, refusing to prey on the minds of others for as long as they can deny themselves.

### Hearteaters and Other Exalted

A Hearteater inherits the memories of her Exaltation’s predecessors, and the most vivid among them are the memory of the Hearteaters’ betrayal at the hands of the Exalted Host. Each Hearteater has their individual reaction to these memories, but the majority have exhibited animosity or outright vendetta against those Exalted. The Bureau of Destiny and the Silver Pact both have extensive institutional knowledge of the Hearteaters, though younger Lunars and Sidereals may never have heard of them. Hearteaters are among the few threats great enough to unify the Sidereals and Lunars; both know that leaving a Hearteater unchecked will result in an existential crisis. Killing a Hearteater permanently is a challenging ordeal, but Lunars and Sidereals working together have succeeded in isolating them from their pawns, pursuing Hearteater Exaltations through multiple consecutive reincarnations, and imprisoning living Hearteaters.

At the height of the Shogunate, Dragon-Blooded sohei of the Immaculate Faith patrolled the world’s edge for Hearteaters, raising the Wyld Hunt against them and leading the attack. In modern times, the Realm and Lookshy are too far to have had any significant interaction with Hearteaters, and the relevant portions of the Immaculate Texts have faded into scholarly obscurity. Ever since the Exaltation of the first Sovereign of Uluiru (p. XX), the Hearteaters across the Northwest

EX3

have been called to the wellspring of their divine patron’s blood that lies beneath the city. It is their ambition to reclaim the Fount of Glories — whether to bathe themselves in Aurora’s blood, hoard it as a relic of his passing, or simply take it from those they deem unworthy. The Sovereigns know little of the Hearteaters’ true nature, but they know enough to fear them, taking extensive countermeasures against infiltration.

### Traits

Hearteaters are intended for Celestial play (p. XX). Anima

The Hearteater’s anima begins as a billowing mist of pale colors, most commonly opalescent blues and greens. As it grows, it becomes an aurora trailing in ribbons that pulse like swollen arteries. Hearteaters’ iconic animas may take the form of monstrous but beautiful horrors, masked or faceless legions, or predatory or parasitic animals, etc. These visual manifestations are typically accompanied by displays of sound: the haunting peal of crystalline bells, the frenzied prayers of the Hearteater’s pawns, a rumbling growl at the very edge of human hearing, etc.

Anima Effects

Hearteaters can spend one mote to perform one of the following effects:

• Discern the precise time of day and the locations of any auroras within (Essence x50) miles. • Sense the direction and approximate distance to one of their pawns.

They also have access to the following anima powers: Gaze Upon Me: For five motes, add (higher of Essence or 3) non-Charm dice on an inspire or instill roll that causes others to experience, value, or understand the Hearteater’s emotions. Resisting the influence requires citing at least a Minor Intimacy in a Decision Point and spending one Willpower. Those with Ties toward the Hearteater must cite an Intimacy of equal or greater value to resist. At bonfire, this power is free. Queen Takes Pawn: For 10 motes and one Willpower, the Hearteater may attempt to claim a mortal human as a pawn. The Willpower cost is waived against trivial characters. The target’s Willpower can’t exceed (higher of Hearteater’s Essence or 3) and he must have a Major or Defining Tie to her or something closely associated with her, like a kingdom she rules or a

heterodox Immaculate theology she preaches. She rolls ([Charisma or Manipulation] + [Occult, Performance, or Presence]) with (her target’s Intimacy) non-Charm successes as a unique influence roll against his Resolve. If she succeeds, she claims him as a pawn. If she fails, she can’t use this power on him again for the rest of the story.

Ravening Horror Pursuit: For three motes, add (higher of Essence or 3) non-Charm dice on a roll to track a character that the Hearteater could make a pawn, or on a roll to navigate to a location populated by potential pawns. While tracking a group of at least a dozen potential pawns or navigating to a city-sized settlement, the bonus is converted to non-Charm successes.

Pawns

A Hearteater’s pawns gain Defining Ties of loyal subservience to her, which can’t be weakened or altered by any means. They are also incapable of voluntarily forming or strengthening negative Ties toward the Hearteater, although existing Ties linger and other characters can instill such Intimacies with influence rolls. The Hearteater can always communicate with her pawns, mind-to-mind, regardless of distance, and they can make influence rolls through this connection. The Hearteater can persuade a pawn to perform an inconvenient task (Exalted, p. 216) without needing to roll. By meditating, the Hearteater can assume total control over a pawn within (Essence x5) miles, making his senses her own and controlling him in body and mind. The Hearteater’s overriding influence is depicted by having her player control all that character’s actions. The pawn’s mental and social actions use the Hearteater’s dice pools and static values, while physical actions use the pawn’s dice pools and static values. Any dice over the Hearteater’s (Attribute + Ability + specialty) or any static value bonuses over her base value count as Charm dice, potentially preventing her from using a pawn’s full dice pool. Her control lapses if the pawn goes beyond (Essence x5) miles from her. While controlling a pawn, the Hearteater doesn’t suffer any damage or negative effects that her pawn does, although she still suffers his wound penalties and penalties from other physical negative effects on actions taken through him. Influence rolls and other effects that target the mind apply to the controlling Hearteater rather than the pawn. The Hearteater’s own wound penalties also penalize her actions through the pawn, as do any other penalties that would impede her ability to focus her mind and exert mental domination

EX3

over her pawn. If a pawn is incapacitated while being controlled, the Hearteater suffers a mental backlash, taking (10 – her Resolve) dice of bashing damage, ignoring Hardness. If a controlled pawn dies, she suffers (15 – her Resolve) damage dice.

Hearteaters can’t use their Charms or other magic through pawns unless they specify otherwise or she has Heart-Eaten Avatar (p. XX). If she has the Charms to claim supernatural beings as pawns, she can use their magic while controlling them, paying the costs with the pawn’s resources.

A Hearteater may have up to (Essence + Willpower) pawns at any one time, with Charms like Becoming the Multitude (p. XX) increasing this limit. Charms like Caging the Wayward Wren (p. XX) expand the range of possible pawns she can claim beyond mortal humans. Being a pawn is a Psyche effect. Magic capable of exorcising possessing spirits, such as Burning Exorcism Technique (Exalted, p. 356) can also free pawns. Recognizing a pawn’s condition for what it truly is requires a difficulty 3-7 (Perception + Occult) roll, with the precise difficulty varying based on the observing character’s background, specialties, and familiarity with the pawn, as well as any relevant facts introduced with Lore rolls. A liberated pawn retains his Defining Tie toward the Hearteater, but it can now be weakened. Martial Arts

Hearteaters aren’t restricted by the Terrestrial keyword, but neither do they have any access to the Mastery keyword.

Sorcery

Hearteaters are capable of initiating into the Terrestrial and Celestial Circles of sorcery.

Evocations

Hearteaters are resonant with adamant (p. XX), and neither resonant nor dissonant with any of the magical materials (Arms of the Chosen, p. 16). Great Curse

The Hearteater’s Great Curse manifests through their unslakable hunger for adulation and attention. They have a Limit track and experience Limit Breaks. Like most Exalted, they gain Limit when they violate a Major or Defining Intimacy (p. XX). They have a shared Limit Trigger, gaining Limit when they go too long without claiming a pawn. The frequency with which they must do so increases as their Limit rises. The specific requirements can be tailored to the

amount of emphasis the play group wants to give a Hearteater player character’s hunger. Animals and other non-sapient pawns are less satisfying than people, requiring a Hearteater to take such pawns more frequently to stave off Limit. Past a certain amount of Limit, they no longer provide any benefit. Mindless pawns, like zombies, never prevent Limit. Concepts for Hearteater Limit Breaks include: The Devourer Unleashed: The Hearteater can no longer contain her monstrous hunger. She must take any opportunity she can to claim a pawn, capable of sparing only those she has positive Ties toward. She waives the cost to do so.

Look Upon Me: The agony of the Hearteater’s hunger pangs drives her to degrade herself by feeding on paltry fare. She must seek out the attention of others, whether it takes the form of worship, adulation, love, hate, fear, or other passions.

Slavering Horror Contagion: The Hearteater’s rapacity spills over into her pawns. They suffer mental corruption related to or thematically associated with one of the Hearteater’s Intimacies that’s relevant to her hunger or recent narrative events involving it. The Hearteater’s control can’t override this corruption. Thousand Faces Blight: The Hearteater’s starved delirium blurs the boundaries between her and her pawns. She’s infected with emotions, memories, and Intimacies from them, or the inhuman mindset of pawns that are animals, strange spirits, and the like. Alternatively, if your playgroup wants to deemphasize their monstrous hunger or give a Hearteater play character greater latitude in dealing with it, you can use a roleplay-based Curse (p. XX).

Longevity and Death

Hearteaters are thought to be as long-lived as the Aurorals, with lifespans of up to three thousand years — though none have ever died of old age. Upon a Hearteater’s death, her Exaltation transmigrates to a human pawn within (Essence) miles. The twisted echo of Aurora’s will that guides her Exaltation chooses a pawn with both heroic potential and an emotional and mental compatibility with her.

The Hearteater’s mind clashes with the newly Chosen pawn’s, struggling for dominance. Typically, neither can conclusively overcome the other, resulting is a gestalt of the two that is essentially a new individual.

EX3

When one does predominate, they subsume the other’s consciousness into their own, remaining themselves, though not entirely unchanged.

There’s no dice roll for the conflict between Hearteater and pawn. Hearteater player characters are assumed to always predominate, unless their player wants to start over with a new character. A predominating Hearteater’s player may reallocate her Physical Attribute dots to better reflect the pawn’s physical abilities, as magnified by Exaltation. She loses any mutations and is refunded their experience cost. Her other traits remain unchanged. At the Storyteller’s discretion, she may take on some of the subsumed Pawn’s Intimacies or gain a Derangement reflecting the effects of absorbing his psyche.

A predominating pawn’s Exalted power manifests in her traits like a newly Exalted Solar’s (Exalted, p. 125). He doesn’t retain the Essence rating or any other supernatural powers of the preceding Hearteater, though he may gain Intimacies or a Derangement from absorbing her, as above. If the two form a gestalt, the new individual that arises from it uses character creation similar to that for newly Exalted Solars. If a Hearteater dies without any pawns within range, her Exaltation does not pass on. Its Essence is caged in her bones, transforming them to opal and rendering them imperishable. The Exaltation passes onto the first mortal to touch the bones. There is no clash of wills with the dead Hearteater, though one only recently dead may manifest strongly among their successor’s past lives.

## Hearteater Charms

Hearteaters both exploit and empower their pawns, amassing thralls to serve as implements of her will. Their monstrous power preys on their enemies’ Intimacies and emotions, but has an eerie beauty to it.

### Excellencies

Hearteaters don’t have formalized Excellencies; they can add dice to any (Attribute + Ability) roll or increase any static value for which they have an applicable Ability at 3+ or an Attribute at 5, paying one mote per die. They may add up to (Attribute + 1) dice to rolls. Actions that uphold one of the Hearteater’s Intimacies or exploit an opposing character’s Intimacy increase this by (Intimacy). Automatic successes count as two dice towards this limit. Static values such as Evasion or Resolve can be raised by half this dice cap, rounded down.

## The Umbral Exalted

A fisherwoman watches the night sky on the beach, nursing bitterness over her meager lot in life. An artist stalks his rival along shadowed alleyways, bearing a long knife that will free him from being second best. A prince sees conspiracies behind every corner, terrified by the poisoners and assassins she imagines in her court. Such inner turmoil, together with the potential for heroism, is the soil in which Umbral Exaltation takes root, a black rose that blooms from the heart’s darkness.

Every Umbral is haunted by her Shadow, a twisted reflection born from her darkest thoughts, worst impulses, and the lingering echoes of the dead god who chose her. It whispers to her, urging her to listen, to heed its counsel, to give in. In exchange, it offers power. The Umbral Exalted are mighty, controlling darkness and shadow by will alone and drawing forth the monstrous passions of others, but to attain the apex of their power they must surrender control to their Shadow, inch by inch, until they can no longer defy it. The Umbrals’ path is a difficult one; each bears their burden differently. Some seek to chain their Shadow, following rigid codes of morality or cultivating discipline through asceticism and austerities. Others let their Shadow slake its wrath against those they deem wicked, channeling their dark passions towards ends they can justify. Still others give their Shadow all that it asks, willing to make any sacrifice or commit any sin if it will bring them power. Some have tried to make peace with their Shadow, forging a symbiotic relationship by understanding and accepting it, though few, if any, have succeeded in this.

### Nebiru, the Lord of Things Unseen

In Creation’s first, myth-dimmed days, the dour and cryptic Nebiru was counted among the Celestial Incarnae, the god of the vast yet invisible planet that bears his name. He was called the Lord of Things Unseen, the Subtle One, He Who You Know Not. Together with his sibling Incarnae, he oversaw the order of Creation, lending them his cunning, his grim resolution, and his insight into the darker nature of gods and mortals alike.

When the gods rose up against their makers, Nebiru refused. He feared the wrath of the world’s creators — and even more so, he feared the diminishment he saw in his kin after they created their Exalted. Jupiter

foresaw what would come of Nebiru’s treachery and convinced her fellow Incarnae to turn against him. Nebiru was rent limb from limb and, still living, interred within his own planet, which still hangs invisible against the night sky. Thus did the Lord of Things Unseen become the First Forbidden God. Millennia passed as Nebiru raged against his prison, cursing the names of his siblings. While the First Age flourished across Creation, the Subtle One struggled endlessly against the bars of his gaol, yet he lacked the power to break what the other Incarnae had wrought. Finally, in an act of utter desperation, he did that which he had sworn never to do: he created Exalted. He poured himself heedlessly into the act that had diminished his kin, never stopping even as it burned him to nothingness. Thus did the Umbral Exalted come into Creation, and thus did Nebiru finally find his freedom in death.

Yet while the Lord of Things Unseen had been destroyed, something of him remained. The Umbral Exalted are the Chosen of Nebiru, and the will that chooses them still endures. An Umbral’s Shadow is born of the darkest aspects of their psyche, but at its heart is a splinter of his Essence, a night bird perched in a nest of doubt, fear, and hatred. In time, Nebiru’s Chosen may yet be his rebirth.

### Umbrals and Other Exalted

The Umbrals have always been few in number and have never united in any large-scale coalition, making their interactions with other Exalted more dependent on the personalities and reputations of those involved rather than the standing of the Umbrals as a whole in the eyes of the great Exalted factions. They were obscure even in the First Age, little encountered and less understood by their fellow Chosen. Some of the Old Realm’s savants studied them and understood that they were fellow Exalted; a few even drew the connection between the Umbrals and the ancient tales of Nebiru the Traitor. But with the Umbrals’ small numbers, few other Exalted of the First Age took interest in this scholarship, even those who counted Umbrals among their allies or enemies.

In the Second Age, the Umbrals are even more obscure. The Realm, Lookshy, and other Dragon-Blooded polities, like the Shogunate before them, have essentially no knowledge of the Umbrals save for that gleaned by Dragon-Blooded who’ve encountered them, and perhaps any wisdom to be found in lost First Age texts that their savants might uncover. Immaculate doctrine

EX3

does not label them Anathema, though an individual’s deeds may earn them that title.

The Bureau of Destiny notionally has access to knowledge of the Umbral Exalted — Lytek, God of Exaltation, chronicles them as diligently as he does any other Exalt, and there are ancient records that have been buried beneath paperwork for centuries — but the vast majority of Sidereals have never had any need to plumb these secrets. Likewise, while a few in the Silver Pact have knowledge of the Umbrals, either from their own lifetime or past life memories, encounters are rare enough that most Lunars may not ever realize their fellow Pact members have insights to offer.
